title: Consultant, Management Systems & Compliance
description:
**ERM**
is the world’s largest specialist sustainability consultancy, with over 50 years of experience helping organizations navigate complex environmental, social, and governance challenges. We bring together a global community of experts to deliver meaningful impact for our clients and the planet.
  
  
Our
**Consulting Delivery Hub**
(CDH) in India is a critical part of ERM’s global consulting model enabling scalable, high-quality delivery across regions and service lines. CDH teams work in close partnership with regional consultants to support global client projects, providing specialist expertise, driving consistency, and enhancing delivery efficiency across our most important programmes.
  
  
As part of the Consulting Delivery Hub, you will collaborate with colleagues worldwide, contribute to complex sustainability projects, and play a key role in shaping the future of global consulting delivery.
  
  
**Why this role matters?**
As a
**Consulting Senior Associate – Management Systems & Compliance**
, you will support ERM's global consulting delivery by assisting in the execution of management system development, legal obligation research, permit and plan preparation, and compliance program tasks. Working within the Safe & Sustainable Operations (SSO) service line, you will work with senior consultants and global teams to deliver reliable, high-quality outputs on client projects. This role focuses on hands-on execution, data handling, documentation, and QA/QC support. It is an excellent opportunity to build a strong foundation in EHS/ESG management systems, regulatory compliance, and digital compliance platforms, while contributing indirectly to global client engagements and to the growth of the CDH-SSO team.
  
  
**What your impact is?**

* Support management system development and implementation support, by assisting with discrete legal registers, legal obligation research, compliance calendars, checklists, and simple governance tools.
* Support digitally enabled delivery of industry-standard EHS/ESG platforms such as Cority, Enablon, Sphera, Intelex, and similar systems.
* Contribute to EHSS permit, plan, and program development and to multi-site compliance program management under the guidance of experienced consultants.
* Support assigned workstreams while maintaining quality and timeline commitments; keep trackers, evidence files, and status reports current.
* Collaborate with global colleagues and CDH-SSO team members, actively participating in learning initiatives and knowledge-sharing activities.

**What will you bring?**

* Bachelor's degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, chemical engineering, occupational health and safety, information systems, or related discipline; equivalent experience considered.
* Typically, 1+ years of relevant experience (including consulting experience) in EHS/ESG management systems, compliance, environmental management, or a related area.
* Basic understanding of H&S software implementation skills, EHS/ESG concepts, management system frameworks, permits, legal registers, and compliance obligations.
* Strong attention to detail and document control discipline; ability to follow instructions, templates, and project workflows.
* Ability to manage assigned tasks, meet deadlines, and produce quality outputs with support from stakeholders.
* Good written and verbal communication skills for preparing documentation and collaborating with global teams.
* Proficiency in MS Office tools (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and good data organization skills; familiarity with EHS/ESG platforms.

**Preferred Qualifications, Skills & Competencies**

* Master's degree in environmental management, sustainability, EHS, environmental policy, information systems, or related fields.
* Exposure to EHS/ESG compliance platforms and trackers such as Cority, Enablon, Sphera, Intelex, legal registers, or compliance calendars.
* Familiarity with ISO 14001, ISO 45001, and international EHS regulatory frameworks such as Clean Air Act, RCRA, OSHA, or other H&S implementation tools.
* Interest in digital, automation, or AI-enabled tools that improve compliance delivery (e.g., Power BI, Power Automate, SharePoint).
* Prior internship or project experience in an EHS/consulting environment.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Support development and implementation of management system elements, including procedures, manuals, legal registers, compliance calendars, and operating procedures.
* Help prepare EHSS permits, plans, programs, and other compliance deliverables.
* Assist in configuring, updating, and maintaining data on EHS/ESG compliance platforms such as Cority, Enablon, Sphera, or Intelex, as required.
* Assist with legal obligation research and regulatory tracking under frameworks such as ISO 14001/ISO 45001, Clean Air Act, RCRA, Clean Water Act/NPDES, or EPCRA, with guidance from senior consultants.
* Assist in maintaining compliance platforms, digital tools, and reporting frameworks by updating data, generating reports, and supporting basic dashboard maintenance.

title: Human Resources Compliance Manager
description:
**Company Description**
KORE SERVICES SECURITY PRIVATE LIMITED is a security services organization headquartered in Delhi, India. The company operates in a dynamic urban environment, supporting clients with reliable security and related support services. As an employer, KORE SERVICES SECURITY PRIVATE LIMITED offers opportunities to work closely with operational teams and corporate management. Team members are encouraged to contribute to efficient, compliant, and professional business practices as the company grows its presence in the region.

**Role Description**
The Human Resources Compliance Manager is a full-time, on-site role based in New Delhi. This role is responsible for developing, implementing, and monitoring HR policies and procedures to ensure compliance with applicable labor and employment laws and internal company standards. Daily activities include reviewing HR processes, conducting compliance audits, maintaining documentation, and advising management and HR staff on regulatory requirements and best practices. The manager will handle employee-related compliance issues, support investigations, coordinate training on HR and compliance topics, and collaborate with legal or external advisors when necessary. The role also involves preparing reports for leadership, updating policies in response to regulatory changes, and promoting a culture of ethical conduct and fair treatment across the organization.

**Qualifications**

* Strong Human Resources (HR) foundation, including experience with HR operations and employee lifecycle management.
* Proficiency in Regulatory Compliance, with the ability to interpret and apply relevant laws, rules, and internal standards.
* Experience drafting, implementing, and maintaining HR Policies that support consistent, fair, and compliant practices.
* Knowledge of Labor and Employment Law, including local, state, and national requirements.
* Excellent analytical, documentation, and reporting skills, with attention to detail and accuracy.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills for collaborating with management, HR staff, and employees at all levels.
* Ability to manage multiple compliance initiatives, work independently on-site, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Law, Business Administration, or a related field; professional HR or compliance certifications are beneficial.

title: Company Secretary
description:
**1. Job Purpose**

The Company Secretary (AM/DM) will be responsible for managing secretarial activities, corporate governance, and regulatory compliances for a listed company. The role requires strong working knowledge of the Companies Act, 2013, SEBI regulations, stock exchange filings and disclosures, Board and shareholder meeting compliances, statutory records, and corporate actions.

The position will involve coordination with regulatory authorities, NSDL/CDSL, stock exchanges, the Registrar of Companies (ROC), Registrar and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs), auditors, and other key stakeholders to ensure timely and accurate compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.

**2. Key Responsibilities**

**A. Secretarial Compliance and Meetings**

* Manage end-to-end secretarial compliances under the Companies Act, 2013, and applicable rules.
* Coordinate and manage Board Meetings, Committee Meetings, Annual General Meetings (AGMs), and Extraordinary General Meetings (EGMs).
* Prepare meeting agendas, notes, minutes, resolutions, and related documentation.
* Ensure timely filing of statutory forms and documents with the Registrar of Companies (ROC).
* Maintain statutory registers, records, and other secretarial documentation.

**B. SEBI and Stock Exchange Compliance**

* Ensure compliance with SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and other applicable SEBI regulations.
* Monitor compliance with SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015.
* Handle applicable compliances under SEBI regulations relating to share-based employee benefits and sweat equity, and substantial acquisition of shares and takeovers.
* Manage stock exchange filings and disclosures with NSE and BSE.
* Coordinate corporate actions and ensure timely submission of required disclosures and regulatory information.

**C. Stakeholder Coordination and Corporate Governance**

* Coordinate with NSDL/CDSL, Registrar and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs), auditors, stock exchanges, and regulatory authorities.
* Support implementation and monitoring of corporate governance requirements.
* Ensure accurate and timely regulatory reporting.
* Liaise with internal stakeholders to obtain information and complete compliance activities within prescribed timelines.

**D. Documentation and Transaction Support**

* Assist in drafting and reviewing corporate documents, policies, resolutions, and regulatory submissions.
* Maintain accurate statutory records and secretarial documentation.
* Support due diligence, fundraising, restructuring, and other corporate transactions, wherever applicable.
* Ensure proper documentation and record-keeping for corporate and regulatory matters.

**E. Compliance Monitoring**

* Monitor the organization’s compliance management software and track compliance status across functions.
* Coordinate with relevant users and departments to ensure timely reporting and closure of compliance requirements.
* Maintain compliance calendars and monitor regulatory deadlines.
* Identify pending compliances and follow up with stakeholders to minimize compliance risks.

**3. Educational and Professional Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in commerce and/or LLB.
* Must be a Qualified Company Secretary and a member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI).

**4. Experience and Technical Competencies**

* 4–5 years of relevant experience in company secretarial, corporate governance, and regulatory compliance functions.
* Experience working with a listed company or a reputed corporate secretarial firm handling listed entity compliances.
* Strong knowledge of the Companies Act, 2013, SEBI regulations, and stock exchange compliance requirements.
* Experience in Board and Committee Meetings, shareholder meetings, statutory filings, and corporate disclosures.
* Proficiency in MS Office and MCA, SEBI, and stock exchange portals.
* Ability to manage multiple regulatory timelines and compliance calendars effectively.

**5. Key Skills and Competencies**

* Strong drafting, documentation, and communication skills.
* Sound understanding of corporate governance and regulatory frameworks.
* Excellent coordination and stakeholder-management abilities.
* Strong attention to detail and accuracy in regulatory filings.
* Effective time management and ability to meet strict compliance deadlines.
* Analytical and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism.

**6. Role Expectations**

The successful candidate will ensure effective management of secretarial and regulatory compliances, maintain high standards of corporate governance, support timely statutory filings and disclosures, and coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure adherence to applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

title: Land Access Manager
description:
**ERM**
is the world’s largest specialist sustainability consultancy, with over 50 years of experience helping organizations navigate complex environmental, social, and governance challenges. We bring together a global community of experts to deliver meaningful impact for our clients and the planet.
  
  
Our
**Consulting Delivery Hub**
(CDH) in India is a critical part of ERM’s global consulting model enabling scalable, high-quality delivery across regions and service lines. CDH teams work in close partnership with regional consultants to support global client projects, providing specialist expertise, driving consistency, and enhancing delivery efficiency across our most important programmes.
  
  
As part of the Consulting Delivery Hub, you will collaborate with colleagues worldwide, contribute to complex sustainability projects, and play a key role in shaping the future of global consulting delivery.
  
  
**Why this role matters?**
As a
**Land Access Manager**
, you will support ERM's global consulting delivery by leading the coordination, negotiation, and management of land access, wayleaves, licenses, and voluntary agreements required to progress UK capital projects through survey, consenting, construction, and post-consent phases. You will work within the Capital Project Delivery (CPD) — Projects Feasibility, Planning & Consents pillar, partnering with UK regional planning teams, project managers, ecology and heritage specialists, and developer/utility clients to deliver secure, timely, and cost-effective access to third-party land. This role is critical to unlocking programme certainty, de-risking consenting and construction, and building CPD's UK Land Services capability as an integrated part of ERM's wider Land & Right of Way offer.
  
  
**What your impact is?**

* Land access is secured on schedule across a portfolio of UK infrastructure and energy projects (transmission, renewables, water, transport, and consented developments), removing critical path risk from survey and construction programmes.
* Landowners, tenants, occupiers, and agents are engaged professionally and consistently, protecting ERM's and our clients' reputation and maintaining social licence to operate.
* Access agreements, wayleaves, option agreements, licences, and heads of terms are drafted, negotiated, and executed to a high commercial and legal standard, in line with client mandates.
* Land referencing, Book of Reference, and Land Interest data are accurate, auditable, and DCO/CPO-ready, integrated with GIS and project data systems.
* Land Access Coordinators and Survey Coordinators within the sub-team are mentored, developed, and deployed effectively, contributing to CPD's UK Land Services growth ambitions.
* The service line grows profitably through repeat business, cross-sell into ERM's ESIA, consenting, and TDD offers, and disciplined utilisation and margin management.

**What will you bring?**

* Demonstrable experience (typically 7+ years) in land access, land referencing, wayleaves, or right-of-way acquisition on UK linear infrastructure, energy, utilities, or major development projects.
* Proven ability to lead landowner negotiations end-to-end — from initial engagement through to signed agreement, damage settlement, and post-works reinstatement.
* Working knowledge of the UK legal and regulatory framework for land access, including the Electricity Act 1989, New Roads and Street Works Act, Planning Act 2008 (DCO), Compulsory Purchase, and voluntary wayleave regimes.
* Experience delivering land referencing outputs to support DCO, TWAO, s.36, or planning applications, including Book of Reference and Land Plans.
* Strong stakeholder management skills across landowners, agents, solicitors, statutory undertakers, and client project teams.
* Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects, budgets, and workstreams to time, cost, and quality — with commercial awareness of utilisation, margin, and negative variance management.
* Confident user of GIS, land data platforms, and Microsoft 365; comfortable interpreting title, deeds, and plans.

**Preferred Skills & Competencies**

* Experience on Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects (NSIPs), offshore transmission onshore works, or large renewables portfolios.
* Prior line management or team leadership experience within a consultancy, developer, or utility land team.
* Familiarity with post-consent land activities including construction access, crossings, and reinstatement.
* Exposure to global delivery or shared service environments, with experience working alongside offshore/CDH delivery teams.
* Experience using automation, GIS-linked land databases, or AI-enabled tools for land referencing and stakeholder tracking.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the land access workstream on assigned UK CPD projects, owning strategy, programme, budget, and risk for landowner engagement, access agreements, and wayleaves.
* Negotiate and secure voluntary access agreements, options, licences, and wayleaves with landowners, tenants, and their agents, in line with client mandates and ethical standards.
* Manage and quality-assure land referencing outputs (Book of Reference, Land Interest schedules, Land Plans) to support DCO, TWAO, and planning submissions, coordinating with GIS and consenting leads.
* Act as the primary interface between ERM project teams, client project managers, external legal advisers, and landowners/agents, ensuring clear, timely, and professional communication.
* Provide input into feasibility, routing, and consenting decisions by flagging land access risks, constraints, and mitigation options early in the project lifecycle.
* Ensure compliance with ERM's health, safety, quality, and ethics standards on all fieldwork and landowner engagement, including lone-working and land access risk assessments.
* Maintain accurate records, audit trails, and evidence of engagement to support future consent examinations, compulsory purchase inquiries, or dispute resolution.

title: Senior Corporate Counsel, Litigation & Regulatory
description:
**Description**
We are seeking an experienced litigation lawyer to join our India Legal team as Senior Corporate Counsel (SCC). In this role, the SCC will independently manage a large and diverse portfolio of contentious matters — spanning commercial arbitrations, civil suits, consumer disputes, and high-stakes regulatory and enforcement proceedings. You will be a trusted advisor to the business, driving litigation strategy, managing risk, and protecting the company's interests across a complex and fast-moving legal landscape.
  
  
This is a high-impact, high-ownership role suited to a self-starter who thrives in a dynamic environment, is comfortable handling matters of significant financial and reputational exposure and can balance strategic judgment with hands-on execution.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Litigation portfolio management: Independently manage a high volume of litigation matters end-to-end, including commercial arbitrations, civil and commercial suits, consumer disputes, and regulatory/enforcement actions.
* Strategy & risk assessment: Develop and drive case strategy, assess litigation risk and exposure, and advise business and leadership on potential outcomes, settlement options, and mitigation.
* External counsel management: Select, instruct, and manage external counsel and law firms; control legal spend, review strategy and work product, and ensure cost-effective, high-quality outcomes.
* Regulatory & enforcement matters: Lead responses to regulatory inquiries, investigations, notices, and enforcement proceedings; engage with regulators and authorities as appropriate.
* Stakeholder advisory: Partner with business teams, compliance, and cross-functional stakeholders to provide clear, practical, and actionable legal advice on contentious issues.
* Pre-litigation & dispute resolution: Handle pre-litigation disputes, demand/response notices, and negotiate settlements; explore and drive alternative dispute resolution where appropriate.
* Governance & reporting: Maintain accurate case tracking, prepare litigation reports and risk dashboards for leadership, and ensure timely escalation of material matters.
* Process & knowledge: Contribute to playbooks, standardization of litigation processes, and continuous improvement in how the team manages disputes at scale.

**Basic Qualifications**

* 13+ years of litigation experience
* Bachelor's degree in Law
* Enrolled and in good standing with the Bar Council of India.
* Strong track record in commercial arbitrations, civil/commercial suits, consumer disputes, and regulatory/enforcement matters — gained at a leading law firm and/or a reputed in-house legal team.
* Demonstrated experience independently managing a large volume of contentious matters simultaneously.
* Strong working knowledge of Indian civil procedure, arbitration law, consumer protection law, and the relevant regulatory frameworks.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience working closely with and advising senior executives of an organization or equivalent
* Experience working independently and directly with all levels of legal and business partners or equivalent
* A blend of in-house experience at a large corporation, ideally in a high-volume, fast-paced industry, and experience as a practicing Advocate.
* Experience managing high-stakes, high-value litigation with significant financial or reputational exposure.
* Experience managing external counsel and controlling legal spend across a large docket.
* Excellent judgment, strong written and oral advocacy, and the ability to communicate complex legal risk to non-legal stakeholders.
* Proven ability to work autonomously, prioritize across competing demands, and operate with a high degree of ownership and bias for action.

title: Legal Associate
description:
**Company**
: Onecrest Infra

**Job Title**
: Legal Associate

**CTC**
: 3-5 LPA

**Location**
: Golf Course Road, Gurugram, India (On Site)

**About OneCrest Infra**

OneCrest Infra develops commercial and mixed-use real estate across Delhi NCR and North India. We acquire land, build, lease to corporate occupiers, and sell the completed pre-leased assets to investors. Our portfolio includes multiple Commercial and Healthcare developments mainly in North India .

Every one of those transactions runs on paper — title chains, land records, agreements to sell, lease deeds, contractor agreements. This role is the in-house owner of that paper.

**What This Role Actually Is**

This is a
**property-focused**
role, not a general corporate compliance job. You will spend most of your time reading land records, assembling document sets, drafting agreements, and coordinating with our external counsel.

Formal title opinions on acquisitions are issued by our external law firm. Your job is to do the
**first pass**
— pull and read the records, build the chain, spot the obvious problems early so we do not waste time and fees on a bad plot, and give external counsel a clean, complete file to work from. You will also draft and manage the bulk of our routine documentation in-house.

You will work directly with the Chairman and with our project, finance, and site teams.

**What Your Ideal Day Would Look Like**

•    Collect, organise, and read the property document set for land and built properties we are evaluating — revenue records, prior deeds, approvals, mutation entries

•    Build the chain of title and prepare a first-pass internal note flagging gaps, encumbrances, pending litigation, and missing documents

•    Identify obvious deal-breakers early and escalate them before we spend further time or money on a site

•    Prepare the complete file for external counsel, brief them clearly, and follow through on their queries until the title opinion is issued

•    Draft and review Agreements to Sell, Sale Deeds, MOUs, and Development Agreements using firm-approved formats — from both buyer and seller side

•    Draft and review
**lease deeds**
for corporate tenants: lock-in, escalation, security deposit, fit-out, exit and renewal terms

•    Draft and review contractor agreements, works contracts, consultancy agreements, and vendor documentation

•    Handle stamp duty computation, registration, and coordination at Sub-Registrar offices across Haryana, Delhi, and Punjab

•    Track regulatory approvals and filings — CLU, licences, HRERA, mutation, EDC/IDC — and keep a live status sheet

•    Support legal notices, recovery correspondence, and dispute matters under the guidance of external counsel

•    Maintain an organised, retrievable record of every contract, deed, notice, approval, and ongoing matter

•    Visit tehsil record rooms, Sub-Registrar offices, and project sites when required

**Eligibility**

**Education**

•    
**LLB**
from a recognised institution

•    Enrolment with a State Bar Council preferred (useful for searches and vakalatnamas, not mandatory)

Experience

•    
**2–4 years**
in property, real estate, or construction legal work — with a developer, a real estate group's in-house team, or a firm with a property practice

•    Hands-on exposure to title document review and property transaction drafting. General corporate or litigation experience alone will not be a fit.

**Must-Have Skills**

**Land Records and Title**

•    Ability to read and interpret
**Revenue records**
: jamabandi, fard, mutation (intkal), khasra–khatauni, aks shajra, girdawari

•    Working knowledge of
**Delhi/NCR property documentation**
: conveyance deeds, GPA/SPA chains and their limitations, freehold vs leasehold, L&DO and DDA processes, MCD mutation

•    Ability to trace a chain of title across successive transfers and identify breaks, gaps, and unexplained transfers

•    Ability to obtain and read encumbrance certificates and run Sub-Registrar index searches

**Regulatory - Haryana and NCR**

•    Working familiarity with all the Authorities including DDA, Noida Authority, the Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975 — licensing, CLU, EDC/IDC

•    Working familiarity with HRERA registration, disclosures, and ongoing compliance

•    Basic understanding of DTCP approvals and building plan sanction processes

**Drafting and Documentation**

•    
**Excellent written English.**
You will draft documents that go to institutional buyers, banks, and corporate tenants. Grammar, clause construction, and precision are non-negotiable and will be tested.

•    Ability to draft a complete agreement from a standard format and adapt it accurately to the facts of the deal

•    Sharp eye for clauses, risks, ambiguity, and inconsistency in documents drafted by the other side

•    Stamp duty and registration procedure across Haryana and Delhi

**Working Style**

•    Organised and reliable — you will be the single point of custody for our documentation

•    Able to run a matter to completion and follow up with external counsel without being chased

•    Comfortable raising a concern early rather than discovering it late

•    Willing to travel within NCR and to Punjab for site and record-room work

**What Will Make You Stand Out**

•    Experience on the seller side of pre-leased or investment-grade asset sales

•    Experience in the know-how of working online with the Govt portals

•    Experience in Lease deeds, sale deeds , ATS and other drafts

•    Prior work on due-diligence in Delhi/NCR

•    Experience with hospital, hotel, or retail chain occupier lease deeds

•    Prior work on land aggregation or acquisition from multiple co-owners or legal heirs

**What's In It For You**

You will be the in-house legal function for a company that transacts constantly. Direct access to the Chairman, visibility on every acquisition, and exposure across the full lifecycle — land purchase, construction contracts, leasing, and exit. You will work alongside a reputed external law firm and learn from their opinions on live deals. As the company grows, this role grows with it.

**Apply**

If you are a property lawyer who reads land records comfortably and drafts cleanly, we would like to hear from you.

**Join OneCrest Infra as a Legal Executive.**

title: AI Architect, Legal OS (AI-Native CLM)
description:
Most enterprise AI never reaches production. Gartner reports that 72% of CIOs are breaking even or losing money on their AI investments. We started Pragyaa to change that.

We build the platform that runs a company's back office on AI: Legal OS, Finance OS, compliance agents, and an ROI dashboard that shows exactly what the AI delivered. Under all of it sits one ontology, a shared model of the business that connects contracts, ledgers, entities and obligations.

This is the kind of result it produces. One of our first agents started at 30% accuracy using a frontier model straight out of the box. We added a knowledge graph and got to 70%. Evals, tuning and a live ERP integration took it to 90%. Today it has audited 600+ certificates on its own and gives a 75-year-old real estate company 20+ hours back every week. We now want to do that for every workflow, in every function, and we need the person who designs the system that makes it repeatable.

What you'll do

You'll architect the platform, write the pieces that matter most, and take work from design through to production:

* Design the core platform: the ontology, connectors, agent runtime, model gateway and evaluation layer shared by Legal, Finance, Compliance and ROI reporting.
* Write the critical code yourself: the ontology layer, extraction pipelines, orchestration and gateway.
* Review and integrate the team's work so every agent works end to end: typed, permissioned, auditable, with human approval where it matters.
* Run evaluation-first engineering: golden datasets from real cases, then continuous improvement on accuracy, cost and latency with every model release.
* Spend about 30% of your time with customers (general counsels, CFOs, compliance heads) turning their hardest workflows into architecture. The other 70% goes into our own platform, so each engagement makes the product stronger.

You might be a fit if

* You've spent 8+ years building software, including 4+ years building AI systems that real enterprise users depend on.
* You've designed a knowledge graph or ontology, and you know when a graph beats vector search and when it's overkill.
* You've shipped LLM agents or document-extraction systems, and you know how to get from 30% to 90% accuracy.
* You think in cost, latency and accuracy together, and you can cut one without breaking the others.
* You're comfortable with cloud platforms, APIs, MCP and messy enterprise systems (ERP, CRM, Microsoft 365, Slack).
* You'd rather ship than write slide decks, and you can explain your trade-offs to a CFO.

Why join us

* You own it: you'll be the architect of the platform, working directly with founders who built AI at Google, AWS, Azure and Meta.
* It's live: our agents already run legal, finance and compliance work for enterprise customers, from a crypto exchange to a 53-year-old retailer. You'll see your work used in production within weeks, not years.
* Results you can measure: every agent you ship reports hours saved and dollar ROI against the customer's own baseline.
* Frontier tools: we're a member of the Claude Partner Network and use AI agents across our own engineering, from spec to code to release.
* Momentum: we're three years in, with $3M+ ARR and 50+ people across the USA, Canada, the EU and APAC, and we're growing fast.

title: Subcontracts Delivery Manager
description:
**The opportunity**
The
**Subcontracts Delivery Manager (SDLM)**
is responsible for the commercial, contractual, and operational management of construction and installation subcontracts on major HVDC projects from contract award through to final completion and closeout.
  
  
The role acts as the primary commercial interface between Hitachi Energy and its subcontractors, ensuring contractual obligations are met while protecting project objectives relating to safety, cost, schedule, quality, and risk.
  
  
Working closely with Construction, Engineering, Project Management, Procurement, Cost Control, and Contract Management teams, the SDLM is responsible for proactively managing subcontract performance throughout project execution. This includes administering subcontract agreements, managing variations and change orders, assessing and resolving claims, negotiating commercial matters, monitoring performance, and identifying risks and opportunities that may impact project delivery.
  
  
A key responsibility of the role is maintaining strong commercial control of subcontract packages. This includes managing payment applications, verifying invoices, tracking costs, preparing reports, supporting cost recovery initiatives, administering contractual changes, and ensuring that all commercial matters are properly documented and managed. The SDLM also plays a key role in the negotiation of final accounts and the successful closeout of subcontracts.
  
  
The position requires strong stakeholder management and communication skills, as the SDLM regularly interfaces with subcontractors, site management, project leadership, engineers, contract managers, and clients. The ability to negotiate effectively, resolve disputes, manage commercial risk, and maintain strong working relationships is critical to success.
  
  
Successful Subcontracts Delivery Managers typically possess extensive experience in construction, infrastructure, energy, utilities, or EPC projects, combined with strong knowledge of contract administration, subcontract management, claims management, change control, commercial management, risk management, and project delivery.
  
  
**How You’ll Make An Impact**

* Manage subcontracts from award and handover through to completion and final closeout.
* Administer subcontract agreements and ensure compliance with contractual obligations.
* Manage variations, change orders, claims, notifications, and contractual correspondence.
* Monitor subcontractor performance, progress, risks, and opportunities.
* Manage payment certification, invoice verification, and cost control processes.
* Support dispute resolution, cost recovery, and final account negotiations.
* Coordinate with project stakeholders to support successful project execution.
* Ensure compliance with contractual requirements, quality standards, health and safety requirements, and company procedures.
* Maintain accurate records, reporting, and commercial documentation.
* Capture lessons learned and contributed to continuous improvement initiatives.
* Responsible to ensure compliance with applicable external and internal regulations, procedures, and guidelines
* Living Hitachi Energy’s core values of safety and integrity, which means taking responsibility for your own actions while caring for your colleagues and the business.

**Your background**
**Education & Experience**

* Relevant third level degree qualification (bachelor’s degree) in Engineering
* 10 Years Experience in heavy / industrial business and preferably in power sector
* Minimum of 5 (five) years in subcontract management experience, this includes commercial, contractual and construction awareness.
* Technical background is advantageous.
* Experience of successfully coordinating and managing multiple subcontracts / tasks effectively.
* Proficient with standard form and bespoke contracts.
* Proficiency in both spoken & written English language is required.

title: Executive Legal Counsel – Employment AP
description:
**Locations**
: London | Gurgaon
  
  
Who We Are
  
  
Boston Consulting Group partners with leaders in business and society to tackle their most important challenges and capture their greatest opportunities. BCG was the pioneer in business strategy when it was founded in 1963. Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact.
  
  
To succeed, organizations must blend digital and human capabilities. Our diverse, global teams bring deep industry and functional expertise and a range of perspectives to spark change. BCG delivers solutions through leading-edge management consulting along with technology and design, corporate and digital ventures—and business purpose. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  
As Executive Legal Counsel, you will serve as the senior-most Employment Legal leader dedicated to BCG’s Asia Pacific (AP) Region, leading the Employment Legal team within AP and advising on the region’s most important and complex employment-related matters. You will provide regional leadership while partnering closely with global Legal colleagues and external counsel .
  
  
You will be a trusted advisor to senior business and HR leaders, embedded in decision-making on complex, high-impact people topics. The role requires not only deep employment-law expertise, but exceptional judgment, stakeholder management and the ability to navigate sensitive issues across different cultures and jurisdictions. As advances in artificial intelligence reshape how organizations recruit, develop, manage and support their workforce, you will help BCG navigate an evolving employment landscape with sound legal judgment, balancing innovation with legal compliance, responsible governance and the firm's values.
  
  
Operating across AP’s diverse legal regimes, cultures and business environments, you will bring together local expertise and regional perspective to help BCG navigate its most complex people matters and implement practical solutions across the region.
  
  

* Your responsibilities will include:
* Lead all Employment Legal matters across AP, covering the full employee lifecycle, including recruitment, performance management, investigations, restructurings and exits.
* Lead and develop BCG’s Employment Legal team across AP, establishing clear roles and accountability, building team capabilities, and fostering a cohesive regional approach while leveraging the local expertise required across AP’s diverse jurisdictions
* Act as the primary regional legal advisor on complex and high-risk employment matters, including litigation, regulatory issues, internal investigations and sensitive employee relations matters.
* Partner closely with senior business leaders and HR to shape decisions that balance legal risk, commercial priorities and an exceptional employee experience.
* Serve as a key Employment Legal partner to AP regional and system leadership, ensuring Employment Legal is engaged early on significant people, organizational and workforce issues
* Advise on emerging workforce issues and technologies, including AI-enabled employment practices, partnering with global Legal, HR and business teams to ensure AP legal and regulatory considerations are reflected in BCG’s approach
* Drive the development and evolution of employment policies and practices to ensure they remain aligned with changing regulatory requirements, evolving workforce expectations and advances in technology.
* Lead Employment Legal support for strategic business and people initiatives across AP, including reorganizations, workforce transformations, acquisitions, divestitures and expansion into new markets.
* Navigate complex cross-border employment issues across AP, identifying common regional approaches where appropriate while recognizing when local legal, regulatory, cultural or employee-relations considerations require differentiated solutions.
* Enhance how employment legal services are delivered by identifying opportunities to leverage legal technology, AI-enabled tools and data responsibly, while ensuring accuracy, confidentiality, consistency and legal defensibility.

What You'll Bring
  
  

* Significant experience in employment law (typically 12–15+ years), with a combination of in-house and leading law firm experience preferred.
* Deep employment-law expertise in one or more major AP jurisdictions, together with significant experience advising on complex employment matters across multiple AP markets. Experience with Japan and/or broader North East Asia and China employment matters would be particularly valuable.
* Exceptional legal judgment and experience managing complex, high-profile employment matters involving significant business impact, reputational and stakeholder considerations.
* Strong understanding of how AI and emerging workplace technologies are reshaping employment law, workforce governance and regulatory expectations.
* Proven ability to influence senior executives and build trusted relationships across a sophisticated, global organization.
* Experience leading and developing high-performing legal teams across jurisdictions and cultures, while fostering collaboration, inclusion and continuous development.
* Proven ability to operate effectively across jurisdictions and cultures, bringing together local experts and stakeholders to develop practical regional solutions.
* Ability to translate complex legal and regulatory issues into clear, practical advice that enables informed business decisions.

Who You'll Work With
  
  
You will join BCG's Legal function and work closely with AP regional and system leadership, senior HR leaders, and colleagues across Legal, Risk, Compliance and the business. You will lead and develop the AP Employment Legal team while partnering closely with BCG’s global Employment CoE and Employment Legal colleagues in other regions.
  
  
You will collaborate with leaders across People, Digital and business teams to navigate evolving employment laws, emerging workforce technologies and organizational transformation. Together, you will help ensure BCG continues to adopt innovative ways of working responsibly, balancing legal compliance, business objectives and an outstanding employee experience.
  
  
Additional info
  
  
At BCG, our people and relationships are at the heart of everything we do. We believe that in-person collaboration plays an important role in our culture, mentorship, and professional development.
  
  
For this role, you will generally be expected to work from a BCG office or in person with clients on a regular basis (typically around 50% of working time), depending on business needs and in line with local policies and practices.
  
  
We aim to provide a dynamic and collaborative environment that fosters connection and teamwork.
  
  
Boston Consulting Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity / expression, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under national, provincial, or local law, where applicable, and those with criminal histories will be considered in a manner consistent with applicable state and local laws.

In this customer facing role, you will focus on AWS Private Pricing Agreements (PPAs) to formulate and close PPAs, coordinate critical phases of simultaneous and multiple deal cycles, and ensure consensus with all relevant stakeholders.
  
  
You will own alignment with C-level executives, IT teams, and multiple lines of business to achieve business outcomes, increase the adoption of AWS services, and to enable private pricing, go-to-market, pan-Amazon, and other strategic relationships.
  
  
Key job responsibilities

* Facilitate alignment and effective AWS communication. Inspire and influence internal stakeholders, experts, and other indirect resources to remove obstacles, resolve conflict for productive engagements.

title: Registrar
description:
Location: Gurugram, India
  
  
Employment Type: Full-time I Onsite
  
  
**About The Role**
The Registrar will provide institutional leadership for academic governance, regulatory compliance, quality assurance, student records, and academic administration This position is responsible for ensuring that the Delhi NCR Campus operates in accordance with applicable Indian higher-education laws and regulations, policies and systems, and the academic, quality, privacy, and administrative standards governing the relevant University’s programmes.
  
  
The Registrar will be responsible for academic policies and procedures and student records and is the key liaison with regulators, faculty, students, parents or guardians, and the University’s leadership. Additionally, the role includes oversight of student compliance and resolution of queries related to academic standing, policies, and institutional requirements. The role will also lead the management of student conduct, disciplinary, academic misconduct, complaints and appeals processes, ensuring fair and consistent application of institutional regulations and procedures.
  
  
The Registrar will be a key interface between The University, systems, and the India Campus, translating institutional standards into effective local processes and maintaining strong working relationships with relevant Indian authorities and University’s role-holders.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Academic Administration**

* Oversee all academic administrative functions including student registration, student support, programme and module maintenance, records management, timetabling, assessment, grading and examinations, stage 1 misconduct, complaint and appeals procedures, data reporting, certification, transcripts, graduation processes, and academic calendar implementation.
* Maintain and safeguard the integrity of institutional data, academic documentation, and student records in accordance with internal policies and applicable laws.
* Ensure the integrity, accuracy and consistency of academic outcomes and qualifications.
* Ensure compliance with professional bodies’ accreditation requirements, where applicable.

**Governance and Compliance**

* Serve as Secretary to key academic governance and statutory committees, ensuring effective governance, record keeping and implementation of decisions.
* Ensure that academic regulations, policies, and procedures are developed, implemented, and reviewed in alignment with applicable Indian requirements and University’s academic governance and quality framework.

**Quality Assurance & Regulatory Compliance**

* Lead the development and implementation of a comprehensive Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness Framework, including internal audits, programme reviews, faculty evaluations, and policy reviews.
* Ensure full compliance with applicable Indian regulatory bodies including the University Grants Commission (UGC), All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), and other relevant authorities.
* Collaborate with the University to ensure alignment of standards, data reporting, and compliance with the UK reporting and quality assurance requirements.
* Prepare and submit all statutory, regulatory, and accreditation-related reports, returns, and audits in a timely and accurate manner.

**Student Compliance & Policy Adherence**

* Develop, communicate and enforce institutional policies related to student codes of conduct, attendance, academic integrity, disciplinary actions, and progression requirements.
* Oversee institutional processes relating to student appeals, complaints, academic misconduct and disciplinary matters, ensuring procedural fairness and regulatory compliance.
* Lead compliance tracking processes for academic eligibility, credit accumulation, progression standards, and degree requirements and address non-compliance issues.

**Resource Allocation**

* Oversee timetabling and facilities allocation for academic purposes to ensure that best use is made of space and equipment.
* Manage the workloads of direct reports to ensure efficient and effective operation and delivery of tasks on schedule.

**Parent and Guardian Liaison**

* Provide oversight of processes relating to parent and guardian queries concerning academic regulations, student records, institutional policies, student conduct and disciplinary matters

ensuring appropriate escalation and adherence to institutional requirements.
  
  

* Maintain confidentiality, professionalism, and empathy in all stakeholder interactions, ensuring alignment with institutional protocols, data protection and privacy policies.

**Institutional Policy, Risk & Legal Oversight**

* Oversee the drafting, implementation, and maintenance of academic policies and standard operating procedures in the context of the University’s quality framework.
* Ensure legal compliance across academic and administrative operations, in collaboration with external legal advisors and university counsel.
* Maintain oversight of academic and regulatory risks identified within the risk register for the campus, ensuring appropriate reporting, mitigation and escalation processes are in place.
* Support internal audits, inspections, and investigations pertaining to academic integrity, operational risk, and institutional performance, as well as requirements of the University’s quality framework.

**Cross-Functional and Strategic Collaboration**

* Work collaboratively with academic leadership, faculty heads, student affairs, admissions, and operations to ensure institutional coherence and accountability.
* Provide strategic guidance in institutional planning, programme development, and policy innovation.
* Represent the University to external regulatory and accreditation bodies, legal fora, and inter- institutional consortia as required.

**Person Specification**
**Professional Experience**

* Significant relevant professional experience, normally including at least 5 years in a senior administrative or regulatory leadership role within a higher education institution.
* Demonstrated expertise in academic governance, regulatory compliance, and policy implementation within Indian higher education.
* Comprehensive understanding of Indian regulatory bodies and frameworks (UGC, AICTE, NAAC, NIRF, etc.).
* F amiliarity with UK higher education standards, Office for Students (OfS) requirements and international regulatory frameworks

**Academic Credentials**

* Master’s degree, doctoral degree, or equivalent qualification in any academic field.
* Demonstrated commitment to professional development in global higher education trends, international compliance standards, and quality assurance frameworks is essential.

**Knowledge and Skill**

* Experience of acting as Secretary to academic governance bodies.
* In-depth knowledge of national and international higher education regulations, academic operations, and institutional accreditation standards.
* Experience of student appeals, complaints, and disciplinary frameworks.
* Knowledge of student records and information governance.
* Strong leadership, planning, and organizational skills with attention to detail and institutional protocols.
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, particularly in high-stakes or sensitive compliance matters.
* Stakeholder management skills, including engagement with students, parents, regulators, and faculty.
* Proven capacity to manage confidential information with integrity and discretion.

title: Associate Corporate Counsel

**Description**
The Associate Corporate Counsel will provide support to litigation counsels in handling labor and employment matters as well as real estate disputes across India. The position is based in Delhi and is for a fixed term of 3 years.
  
  
The role involves assisting with case management and legal proceedings. This includes reviewing cases to understand the facts and circumstances, analyzing applicable laws and regulations, and drafting or reviewing pleadings, notices, and other legal documents required for court proceedings.
  
  
The position requires coordination with outside counsels to ensure effective representation before courts and law enforcement authorities throughout India.

External Counsel Coordination
  
  

* Coordinate with and manage external advocates, law firms and consultants to ensure effective representation.

Court Representation & Dispute Resolution
  
  

* Represent the Company before courts, tribunals, regulators and quasi-judicial authorities, where permitted.

Advisory & Compliance

A day in the life
  
  

* Litigation Management
* Legal Documentation
* External Counsel Coordination
* Advisory & Compliance

* 5+ years of litigation experience
* Experience of a mix of corporate law firm and in-house work

* Candidates with prior litigation experience before courts and tribunals will be preferred.

title: Principal Associate
description:
**ABOUT THE FIRM**

Stride AMC manages multiple Alternative Investment Funds across India (SEBI Cat 2 AIF), GIFT City (IFSCA AIF), ADGM / Abu Dhabi (FSRA Cat 3) and London (FCA-regulated). We invest across debt / equity / credit strategies and partner with high-growth companies across sectors. The legal team is central to everything we do — from regulatory compliance to deal execution to investor management.

The legal team operates as a true business partner — advising the investment team, management and board on the full spectrum of fund, transaction and corporate legal matters.

**ROLE OVERVIEW**

This is a senior, high-impact role for an accomplished lawyer with 6–8 years of post-qualification experience. The Principal Associate will independently lead complex multi-jurisdictional transactions, regulatory compliance and AMC-level strategic legal matters. The role involves significant interaction with senior management, the board, investors, regulators and external counsel. The successful candidate will be a trusted legal advisor within the organisation and will play a key role in building institutional legal processes and managing the broader legal team.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Investor Management & Complex Fund Documentation**

* Lead drafting, review and negotiation of contribution agreements, side letters, limited partnership agreement (LPA) amendments, co-investment agreements and related documents across all fund structures.
* Drive PPM updates, fund rules amendments and constitutional document revisions independently; ensure regulatory alignment across all jurisdictions.
* Advise on complex investor structuring queries, including nominee / custodian arrangements, FDI / ODI considerations, FEMA structuring, tax treaty implications and FATCA / CRS compliance.
* Manage LP disputes, complaints, escalations and redemption/transfer requests, including coordination with the investment team and compliance.
* Lead fund lifecycle events: first close, interim closes, final close, fund extensions, GP-led restructurings, successor fund formation and wind-down processes.

**2. Strategic Transactions, Acquisitions & Structuring**

* Lead the legal workstream on key strategic transactions: fund platform acquisitions, GP stake sales, mergers of fund structures, spin-offs, co-investment platform formation and secondary market transactions.
* Advise on and execute AMC-level transactions: acquisitions of AMC stakes or businesses, joint ventures, management buy-ins/buy-outs and change of control arrangements.
* Structure and execute complex equity transactions: control buyouts, leveraged acquisitions, structured equity, convertible instruments (CCDs, OCDs, OFCDs), rights offerings and exit structures (drag-along, tag-along, put/call options).
* Lead complex debt transactions: structured / mezzanine debt, syndicated facilities, listed NCD issuances (on BSE / NSE), securitisation / ABS transactions, inter-creditor and security trustee arrangements.
* Manage external legal counsel across jurisdictions on complex transactions; review and control external counsel costs against budget.
* Advise the investment team on deal structuring, risk allocation and transaction documentation strategy.

**3. AMC Structuring, Governance & Corporate Legal**

* Advise on AMC-level structural and ownership matters: entity reorganisations, holding company arrangements, regulatory capital requirements, SEBI registration amendments and change of control approvals.
* Support SEBI / IFSCA registration and in-principle approval matters, licence amendments and new product / scheme launches.
* Draft and review internal AMC policies, board papers, governance frameworks, committee charters, conflict of interest policies, code of conduct and related party transaction policies.
* Advise on FEMA / ODI / FDI implications of AMC investments, fund structuring and offshore fund flows.
* Manage complex regulatory enquiries, arbitrations, disputes and litigation with external counsel.

**4. General Counsel Support & Cross-Functional Advisory**

* Act as a senior legal advisor to the investment team, CFO, COO and board — providing timely, high-quality legal advice on cross-functional matters including competition law, ESG / sustainability disclosures, insurance, IP and technology.
* Advise on senior employment matters: key management employment agreements, ESOP, carry structuring and grant processes, retention schemes, non-compete / non-solicitation arrangements and senior employee disputes.
* Lead DPDP Act 2023 (India), UK GDPR and ADGM data protection compliance; manage data processing agreements and privacy incident response.
* Lead complex vendor and technology negotiations: IT infrastructure, fund administration, custody, data and analytics agreements.
* Mentor and supervise the Legal Associates and other junior team members; support capacity building, knowledge management and precedent development.

**QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE**

* LLB / LLM from a recognised institution.
* 6–8 years of post-qualification experience, with significant time at a Tier 1 / Tier 2 law firm in fund formation, structured finance or M&A practice, or in-house at an AMC, fund, NBFC or financial services company.
* Deep expertise in SEBI AIF regulations and fund documentation — this is a mandatory requirement.
* Significant hands-on experience in debt transaction documentation (NCDs, debentures, structured finance, security creation) and equity transaction documentation (SSA, SHA, control deals).
* Demonstrated experience advising on complex or strategic transactions (acquisitions, structuring, fund mergers or GP-led transactions) is strongly preferred.
* Prior exposure to offshore fund structures (GIFT City IFSCA, ADGM / FSRA, FCA-regulated) is a strong advantage.
* Experience advising on AMC structuring, SEBI licence matters or regulatory approvals is a plus.

**KEY SKILLS & COMPETENCIES**

* Independent legal judgment: confident in providing definitive advice without routine escalation.
* Strong commercial acumen: ability to understand business priorities and translate them into pragmatic legal solutions.
* Excellent negotiation skills: able to negotiate effectively with sophisticated counterparties including institutional investors, PE funds, banks and large corporates.
* Stakeholder management: comfortable engaging with board-level stakeholders, regulators, external counsel and international counterparts.
* Leadership and mentoring: able to delegate, guide and develop junior team members.
* Ability to manage multiple high-priority workstreams under tight timelines.
* Resilient and adaptable in a fast-paced, multi-jurisdictional environment.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

title: Compliance Executive
description:
Key Responsibilities – Quality & Compliance (Secretarial and FEMA)

1. Quality Review of Documents

* Review secretarial and regulatory documents before filing to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
* Review incorporation documents, including SPICe+, e-MoA, e-AoA, AGILE-PRO-S, INC-9, DIR-2, registered office proofs, and LLP incorporation forms.
* Review annual ROC filings such as AOC-4, MGT-7/MGT-7A, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC, DPT-3, MSME-1, and LLP Forms 8 and 11.
* Review event-based ROC filings, including INC-20A, INC-22, DIR-12, PAS-3, SH-7, MGT-14, CHG-1, BEN-2, STK-2, and relevant LLP forms.
* Verify board and general meeting notices, minutes, resolutions, statutory registers, and share issue documentation.
* Review FEMA-related filings, including FC-GPR, FC-TRS, LLP-I, LLP-II, Form DI, Form ODI, APR, ECB-2, and FLA returns.
* Verify names, DIN/DPIN, capital details, shareholding, dates, authorised signatories, supporting documents, and attachments against source records.
* Conduct 100% quality checks for high-risk filings, particularly FEMA reporting, share allotments, and charge-related filings, along with defined sampling checks for routine filings.
* Monitor statutory filing deadlines and identify discrepancies that may lead to resubmissions, penalties, or additional fees.

2. Quality Reporting and Founder Coordination

* Report directly to the Founder on quality, compliance risks, and recurring filing errors.
* Prepare weekly quality reports covering filings reviewed, error rates by team and form, resubmissions, and late fees.
* Escalate critical errors or compliance risks promptly and recommend corrective actions.
* Maintain an error log to track discrepancies by team, form type, and root cause.

3. Team Training and Development

* Conduct induction training for new joiners on incorporation, ROC compliance, and FEMA processes.
* Organise monthly refresher sessions based on recurring errors and process gaps.
* Communicate relevant regulatory updates issued by the MCA, RBI, and ICSI, and ensure checklists are updated accordingly.
* Assess team members’ readiness before authorising them to independently handle specific filing types.

4. SOPs, Checklists, and Regulatory Compliance

* Develop and maintain standardised quality-checking checklists for each form and service line.
* Create, review, and update SOPs, templates, and internal quality-control procedures.
* Track amendments to the Companies Act, 2013, LLP Act, 2008, applicable FEMA regulations, and Secretarial Standards.
* Ensure internal processes remain aligned with applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.

5. Process Improvement and Automation

* Identify recurring errors and implement preventive measures to address their root causes.
* Collaborate with delivery teams to improve filing accuracy and operational efficiency.
* Work with the product and technology teams to convert manual checklists into system validations and automated pre-filing checks.
* Exercise quality-control authority to hold or escalate filings that do not meet the required accuracy and compliance standards until the issues are resolved.

title: Analyst – CLM Configuration
description:
**About Sirion**
Sirion is the world’s leading AI-native Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) platform, transforming the way global enterprises manage their contracting journey. Powered by generative AI, Sirion delivers intelligent extraction, conversational search, and AI-driven negotiation capabilities for some of the world’s most valuable brands. With over 7M+ contracts worth nearly $800B under management and recognition from Gartner, IDC, and Spend Matters, Sirion continues to set the benchmark for innovation in CLM.
  
  
www.sirion.ai
  
  
**Power the Future of SaaS Delivery & Why This Role Matters**
As an Analyst – CLM Configuration, you will play a key role in configuring and automating legal contract templates within Sirion’s Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) platform. You will transform approved legal documents and clause libraries into dynamic, reusable templates that enable clients to generate accurate contracts based on predefined business rules and requirements.
  
  
Working closely with clients, legal teams, business stakeholders and internal implementation teams, you will configure template logic, validate contract outputs and ensure high-quality delivery within agreed timelines. This role requires strong attention to detail, logical thinking and an understanding of contract structures, with a focus on accuracy, automation and client satisfaction.
  
  
**How You’ll Make an Impact**
**Contract Template Configuration & Automation**

* Configure approved legal contract templates and clause libraries, including NDAs, MSAs, SOWs, DPAs, purchase agreements and service agreements, within Sirion’s CLM platform.
* Map contract fields, variables and data points to enable automated contract generation.
* Configure clause assembly, conditional logic and fallback clauses based on predefined business rules, contract requirements and approved legal language.
* Support template configuration across different languages, governing laws and jurisdictions, ensuring the appropriate clauses and provisions are applied.

**Template Testing & Quality Assurance**

* Conduct User Acceptance Testing (UAT) to validate template configurations and ensure contracts are generated accurately across different scenarios and combinations of business rules.
* Identify, troubleshoot and resolve configuration issues, inconsistencies and defects in contract outputs.
* Validate template functionality against approved requirements and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to resolve issues before production deployment.
* Maintain quality standards and ensure templates are ready for production within agreed timelines.

**Client Engagement & Delivery Management**

* Participate in client kick-off meetings, template discussions and requirement-gathering sessions to understand business and legal requirements.
* Collaborate with client legal teams, business stakeholders and internal implementation teams to clarify requirements, validate approved clauses and translate business needs into configuration rules.
* Estimate effort and manage assigned templates independently, ensuring timely delivery against agreed project milestones.
* Manage multiple templates and concurrent client engagements, prioritising work effectively while maintaining accuracy and quality.

**Skills & Experience You Bring to the Table**
**Experience & Education**

* 2–5 years of relevant experience in CLM implementation, contract template configuration, document automation or legal technology.
* Hands-on experience configuring contract templates, clause libraries, conditional rules or automated document-generation solutions.
* Experience working with CLM platforms such as Sirion, Icertis, Conga or other comparable contract management solutions is preferred.
* Familiarity with legal contract structures and documents such as NDAs, MSAs, SOWs, DPAs and purchase or service agreements.
* A legal or paralegal background is an advantage.

**Functional & Technical Skills**

* Understanding of contract structures, clause libraries, contract variables and document-generation logic.
* Ability to translate business and legal requirements into configurable template rules.
* Experience with UAT, test scenarios, defect identification, troubleshooting and quality assurance.
* Familiarity with different governing laws, jurisdictions and language-specific contract requirements is an advantage.

**Core Competencies**

* Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy and quality.
* Analytical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret requirements and troubleshoot configuration issues.
* Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate with clients and cross-functional stakeholders.
* Strong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple templates and meet delivery commitments.
* A client-focused mindset and the ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with the wider team.

**Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion**
Sirion is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We do not discriminate based on race, color, gender, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. Reasonable accommodations are provided as required by law.

title: Public Affairs Manager - India
description:
**Quote from Hiring Manager**
Brown-Forman, a longstanding leader in promoting the responsible enjoyment of premium beverage alcohol products, seeks to retain a Public Affairs professional to assist in implementing its strategies to enhance and protect Brown-Forman’s commercial and and marketing freedoms, and promote alcohol responsibility in India.
  
  
**Meaningful Work From Day One**

* Assessing the cultural and political environment affecting the distilled spirits industry in India and providing sound strategic and tactical advice to the company
* Serving as an advocate for Brown-Forman’s interests with State and Central Governments and regulatory departments within India
* Furthering Brown-Forman’s policies as one of its representatives on local industry trade associations and social aspects organizations.
* Cultivate strong partnerships with key stakeholders in Excise, Government and industry on an ongoing basis to maintain the required/desired Public Affairs goals and objectives
* Collaborate regularly with relevant authorities on policies in line with B-F’s organization and business strategy
* Spearhead initiatives to implement recommended policies/amendments

**What You Can Expect**

* Strategically inform, identify and advise Brown-Forman on public policy initiatives to promote industry self-regulation, alcohol education, and alcohol responsibility throughout India
* Contribute to the development of a comprehensive strategy and consistent practice for Brown-Forman government relations for India
* Work closely with B-F local management to develop and implement a proactive agenda to advance Brown-Forman’s commercial interests in India

**This Will Involve**

* Working to protect Brown-Forman’s interests from threats that would worsen the commercial environment for the responsible sale and marketing of distilled spirits
* Identifying and working (most often collectively with others in the beverage alcohol industry) to reform existing laws, policies and regulations that unreasonably impede Brown-Forman’s business in India
* Spokesperson for Brown-Forman on political and alcohol responsibility matters with governments, politicians and regulators
* Advise and provide support on strategic and policy matters in the areas of alcohol responsibility and Public Affairs in India
* Collaborate with the General Manager, India and South Asia and the leadership team to ensure the commercial imperatives for the India business are reflected in India public policy and regulation
* Serve as Brown-Forman’s primary representative on day-to-day matters involving trade associations of which Brown-Forman is a member in India, including ISWAI working groups (International Spirits and Wine Association of India)
* Work closely with and under the guidance and direction of the VP, Director of Public Affairs EAA in determining policy and involvement in all these and other discussion forums
* Support the General Manager, India and South Asia in their capacity as Brown-Forman’s representative on the board of ISWAI
* Coordinate lobbying on behalf of Brown-Forman, including ensuring compliance with the highest ethical standards and all applicable laws and governmental regulations
* Collaborate with internal colleagues in India and abroad (including the General Manager, India and South Asia, legal, supply chain, marketing, commercial and finance) regarding regulatory issues in India
* Coordinate the Responsibility agenda within Brown Forman India
* Drive and monitor policy and program interventions with government & industry bodies across the states, monitoring their progress and follow-up in furtherance of the company's growth plans and business objectives
* Provide timely information on any policy change with its implications to all regions
* Working with the Legal Manager, India, ensures the company’s policy positions are designed and implemented in compliance with relevant laws and company policies
* Keep a watching brief and communicate regularly on competitor positions and policy approaches with government
* Ensure all issues related to State Excise, Licensing, land matters and environment are timely anticipated and resolved
* Establishing, maintaining and developing healthy relationships with the central and state government authorities, Embassy contacts and apex trade bodies (example FICCI, CII, CCPA, ASCI, AmCham) for strategic engagement
* Overseeing all applications for permission / approvals/License / registration
* Working closely with the functional heads and managers, and keeping them well informed on relevant public policy issues, debates and trends; extend guidance and advice on issues involving clearance from Central/State government and statutory/regulatory authorities

**What You Bring To The Table**

* Public Affairs professional with a graduate degree and at least 10 years of applicable experience
* Experience sitting on or working for an industry trade association
* Familiarity with navigating the state and central government political systems in India
* Excellent oral and written communication skills. The successful candidate will be an organized thinker, a good planner and a strong advocate. The candidate must be able to communicate, even on highly complex matters, in short, readable memos
* Ability to influence and lobby successfully for company and industry positions. Brown-Forman places great emphasis on the ability to strategize and persuade; these qualities are fundamental to this position
* Dealing with Ambiguity - handles risk and uncertainty comfortably and has good judgment on how new ideas will play out in the market
* Multicultural mindset
* Team player
* Highest reputation for integrity
* Good judgment. Brown-Forman recognizes that public policy, particularly in the beverage alcohol area, can be sensitive and controversial. The successful candidate will recognize these sensitivities and have demonstrated the ability to use common sense and exhibit balanced thinking
* Ability to set priorities, identify opportunities, and see matters through to successful completion. The successful applicant will be a self-starter capable of managing a variety of projects efficiently with minimal supervision

**What Makes You Unique**

* Experience in the spirits / alcobev industry strongly preferred
* Experience working in a heavily regulated industry within the region
* Understanding of:

○ the operation of excise, tax and customs laws and regulations in India
  
  
○ Food Safety Standards Association of India (FSSAI) labeling requirements
  
  
○ ASCI marketing guidelines and operation of the CCPA
  
  
**Who We Are**
We believe great people build great brands. And we know there is Nothing Better in the Market than a career at Brown-Forman. Being a part of Brown-Forman means you will grow both personally and professionally. You will have the opportunity to solve problems, seize opportunities, and generate bold ideas. You will belong to a place where teamwork matters and where you are encouraged to bring your best self to work.
  
  
**What We Offer**
Total Rewards at Brown-Forman is designed to engage our people to ensure sustainable and profitable growth for generations to come. As a premium spirits company, we offer equitable pay structures for individual and company performance alongside a premium employee experience. We offer a range of premium benefits that reflect our company values and meet the needs of our diverse workforce.

Contract Management Team

title: Company Secretary
description:
**About the Role**

We are seeking a Company Secretary (CS) who responsible for ensuring the organization complies with all applicable statutory, regulatory, and corporate governance requirements. * Oversee statutory filings with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) / Registrar of Companies (ROC), including annual returns, financial statements, director appointments, charges, and event-based e-forms.
* Ensure strict adherence to the Companies Act, 2013, Secretarial Standards issued by ICSI, and other corporate legislations.
* Coordinate and facilitate Annual Secretarial Audits, statutory audits, and internal compliance reviews.

* Manage documentation related to changes in corporate structure, alter Memorandum and Articles of Association (MOA/AOA), and handle registered office changes.
* Advise management on the legal and compliance implications of commercial contracts, joint ventures, mergers, acquisitions, and strategic partnerships.

* Liaise with external legal counsels, regulatory bodies, and authorities during inspections, litigation, or regulatory queries.

**Requirements**

* Qualified Company Secretary and an active Associate/Fellow member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ACS / FCS).
* 2–5 years of post-qualification secretarial experience in a private limited or listed public company.

Job Summary

The ideal candidate should have strong knowledge of the Companies Act, MCA filings, ROC compliance, and corporate governance, along with proven team management and client-handling skills.

* Ensure timely preparation, review, and filing of statutory forms with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) and Registrar of Companies (ROC).

* Track pending filings, identify compliance gaps, and implement processes to minimize delays, penalties, and errors.
* Develop and improve standard operating procedures (SOPs), checklists, reporting mechanisms, and quality-control processes.
* Prepare periodic MIS reports on team performance, filing status, pending cases, and compliance turnaround times.
* Support client escalations and resolve complex compliance-related queries.

* Bachelor's degree in Commerce, Law, Business Administration, or a related field.

* 7–8 years of relevant experience in corporate compliance, ROC filings, and MCA-related activities.

Required Skills

* Strong knowledge of the Companies Act, 2013, MCA regulations, and ROC filing procedures.
* Practical experience with annual filings, event-based filings, and statutory compliance management.

* Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
