**Job Description**

Job Summary

We are seeking a highly experienced
**Senior Manager – Procurement Audit**
to lead procurement audit, governance, compliance, and risk management initiatives across the organization. The role will be responsible for evaluating procurement processes, identifying control gaps, ensuring policy compliance, mitigating commercial risks, and driving process improvements to enhance procurement efficiency and transparency.

The ideal candidate should possess strong expertise in procurement operations, contract management, supplier governance, internal controls, spend analysis, and audit frameworks, preferably within Construction, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Data Centers, Manufacturing, EPC, or Consulting environments.

Key Responsibilities

Procurement Audit & Compliance

* Lead end-to-end procurement audits across projects, corporate functions, and business units.
* Review procurement transactions to ensure adherence to organizational policies and standard operating procedures.
* Evaluate procurement controls, approval matrices, delegation authorities, and compliance frameworks.
* Identify process gaps, control weaknesses, and areas of potential financial leakage.
* Ensure compliance with procurement governance standards and regulatory requirements.

Risk Assessment & Governance

* Conduct periodic procurement risk assessments and recommend mitigation strategies.
* Review procurement practices for fraud risks, conflict of interest, and unethical sourcing activities.
* Establish audit plans based on risk prioritization and business requirements.
* Drive procurement governance initiatives and strengthen internal control mechanisms.

Contract & Commercial Audit

* Audit contracts, purchase orders, and vendor agreements for compliance with approved commercial terms.
* Verify adherence to procurement cycles, tendering processes, and competitive bidding requirements.
* Assess contract deviations, variation orders, and commercial approvals.
* Review supplier claims, price escalations, and procurement spend against approved budgets.

Supplier & Vendor Audit

* Evaluate supplier selection and onboarding processes.
* Conduct vendor compliance reviews and performance audits.
* Assess vendor concentration risks and opportunities for supplier optimization.
* Review vendor documentation, certifications, and contractual compliance.

Data Analytics & Reporting

* Analyze procurement spend data and identify trends, anomalies, and cost-saving opportunities.
* Generate audit reports highlighting findings, observations, risks, and recommendations.
* Present audit findings to senior leadership and stakeholders.
* Track closure of audit observations and corrective actions.

Process Improvement

* Recommend and implement best practices to improve procurement efficiency and transparency.
* Drive automation and digitization initiatives within procurement audit processes.
* Support process standardization across business units and projects.
* Benchmark procurement practices against industry standards.

Stakeholder Management

* Collaborate with Procurement, Finance, Commercial, Legal, and Project teams.
* Guide procurement teams on policy adherence and corrective actions.
* Conduct audit awareness sessions and training programs for stakeholders.
* Support external, statutory, and internal audits as required.

**Qualifications**

Experience

* 10-15 years of experience in Procurement, Commercial Management, Internal Audit, or Procurement Governance.
* Minimum 5 years of experience handling procurement audits and compliance reviews.
* Experience in Construction, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Data Centers, EPC, Manufacturing, or Consulting organizations preferred.
* Proven experience in managing large procurement spends and audit programs.

title: Legal and Compliance Officer
description:
**Role Summary**

Priquant Ventures Private Limited is hiring a Legal & Compliance Officer who will be designated as the Compliance Officer of the Investment Manager under Regulation 20(17) of the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012.

The role owns the fund's regulatory compliance end to end and acts as in-house counsel on fund documents, investor onboarding and portfolio transactions. It is a hands-on position in a lean team, with reporting to the Managing Partner.

Key responsibilities

The officer is accountable for the fund staying compliant with the SEBI Act, the AIF Regulations, the AIF Master Circular and every scheme's PPM, and for the legal soundness of what the fund signs.

SEBI and regulatory compliance

* Act as the designated Compliance Officer of the Investment Manager and monitor compliance with the SEBI Act, AIF Regulations, circulars and directions
* Own the compliance calendar for all schemes: quarterly activity reports to SEBI, unit value reporting to depositories, benchmarking agency data, and other periodic filings
* Prepare the annual Compliance Test Report for the Trustee and Sponsor under the AIF Master Circular
* Coordinate the annual PPM compliance audit, track findings to closure, and file PPM changes with SEBI and investors
* Report material breaches to SEBI, the Trustee and the Board within the prescribed timelines
* Track new SEBI circulars, assess their impact on each scheme, and update internal policies and procedures accordingly
* Monitor investment conditions and restrictions: concentration limits, Category II leverage restrictions, related-party and associate investments, and investor consents where required
* Handle SEBI inspections, queries and correspondence

Fund documentation and launches

* Draft, review and maintain PPMs, contribution agreements, the indenture of trust and investment management agreement
* Run the regulatory process for new scheme launches through merchant bankers and SEBI, including responding to observations
* Maintain unit class terms, side letters and investor-specific arrangements consistently with the PPM

Drafting of agreements and legal documents

* Draft and negotiate agreements across the fund and the Investment Manager: contribution agreements, side letters, investment management and trusteeship agreements, distribution and placement agreements, and venture partner and advisor agreements
* Prepare first drafts of transaction documents, including term sheets, share subscription, shareholders' and share purchase agreements, debenture trust deeds and security documents
* Draft vendor, service provider and outsourcing contracts (RTA, fund accountant, custodian, valuer, technology vendors), NDAs and engagement letters for counsel and auditors
* Draft board and Investment Committee resolutions, minutes, investor notices, consent requests and regulatory correspondence
* Maintain a library of standard templates and clause positions, and keep them current with regulatory changes

Investor onboarding, KYC and AML

* Run investor onboarding: KYC, CKYC uploads, FATCA/CRS declarations, accredited investor checks and minimum commitment validation
* Act as the point person for PMLA obligations, including risk-based due diligence, record-keeping and suspicious transaction reporting through the Principal Officer framework
* Oversee capital call, distribution and transfer documentation; review distributor empanelment and distribution agreements
* Handle investor grievances and SCORES / SEBI ODR complaints

Transaction and portfolio legal support

* Review term sheets, share subscription and shareholders' agreements, share purchase agreements and debt documentation for equity and structured credit deals
* Run legal due diligence with external counsel and track conditions precedent and post-closing obligations
* Review structured credit documentation: PTC and SDI transaction documents, trust deeds, servicing arrangements and security documents
* Monitor portfolio company covenants, information rights and reporting obligations owed to the fund

Governance, conflicts and controls

* Maintain the conflict of interest policy, the code of conduct and personal trading rules for the investment team
* Keep minutes and records for Investment Committee and Board meetings and maintain the statutory registers of the Investment Manager
* Track NISM certification requirements for the key investment team and other associated persons
* Oversee cyber security, data protection and outsourcing compliance, including vendor contracts
* Manage external counsel, auditors, the Trustee, the custodian, the RTA and the fund accountant on legal and compliance matters

Qualifications and experience

The NISM Series-III-C certification is non-negotiable: from 1 January 2027, only certified persons may be appointed as, or continue to act as, Compliance Officer of an AIF manager (SEBI circular, 30 Dec 2025).

**Required**

* Qualified Company Secretary (ACS/FCS) — mandatory; an LLB is an added advantage
* NISM Series-III-C: Securities Intermediaries Compliance (Fund) certification, or willingness to obtain it before joining
* Working knowledge of the SEBI AIF Regulations and Master Circular, PMLA and KYC rules, the Companies Act 2013, FEMA, and the Indian Trusts Act
* Hands-on drafting & review of investment documents, agreements etc.

**Preferred**

* Experience with growth equity or venture transactions: SHAs, SSAs and secondary share purchases
* Exposure to SEBI inspections, PPM audits or scheme launches through a merchant banker

Skills and attributes

We want someone who reads regulations closely and applies them strictly, while keeping the business moving.

* Independent judgement, with the confidence to say no and put it in writing
* Precise, plain-English drafting for regulators, investors and counterparties
* Organised enough to run a multi-scheme compliance calendar without slippage
* Comfortable owning work end to end in a small team, without a large support function
* Discretion with confidential investor and deal information
* Practical with tools: compliance trackers, document management and SEBI/depository portals

**About QCI**

The Quality Council of India (QCI) is the Scheme Owner of the Certification Scheme for Unmanned Aircraft Systems (CSUAS), which was notified in official gazette by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on 26 January 2022. The scheme has since been revised and its scope enhanced, evolving into a Type based certification framework that covers Visual Line of Sight (VLOS) and Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS) UAS operations, and it also promotes the indigenisation and development of the domestic drone industry, contributing to the vision of India becoming a global drone hub by 2030.

**Role Summary**

As part of the team, you contribute to the development and operation of a national certification framework for UAS. Our work spans into designing and developing certification schemes aligned with international best practice, formulating technical standards, and creating certification ecosystems in partnership with industry, regulators, ministries, academia and other stakeholders, scale them through conformity assessment bodies. Deep understanding of the Drone Rules, 2021 and CSUAS is essential.

The next phase of this work is about collaborating with the industry on the segments that still need enabling, namely autonomous drones, Drone-as-a-Service and UAS traffic management, along with the digital transformation that simplifies compliance and the aggregator led facilitation that scales the use-case adaptation to advance the growth of Industry These are areas where the standards, the quality assurance mechanisms and in some cases the market itself are still taking shape, and the people who join us now will help shape the Nation’s Drone Ecosystem.

**Role & Responsibility-**

QCI is seeking professionals to support the implementation of CSUAS. The role will contribute to the development and operation of the CSUAS workstreams below:

* **Scheme Design & Development**
  : Conceptualise UAS related quality interventions that help the industry and the regulator, and develop and revise the scheme criteria, technical standards and guidelines that give them effect with a in-depth understanding of the Drone Rules, 2021 and CSUAS.
* **Research, Analysis & Knowledge Products**
  : Conduct rapid primary and secondary research on UAS domain and policy, including comparative study of standards and international best practice to draft standards for UAS and its components.
* **Report Writing & Deck Preparation:**
  Draft and structure reports, concept notes, technical circulars and knowledge products, and create data driven presentations for relevant stakeholders.
* **Scheme Operations**
  : Lead the day to day operations of the scheme and its projects, scheme documentation, deliverables, work plans, trackers and minutes of meetings and report periodically on developments; collect, clean and analyse scheme data and maintain its records, website and dashboard; propose the features and changes required in the dashboard to support operations; monitor scheme-related activities; coordinate with vendors and internal and external stakeholders; and frequently update FAQs.
* **Stakeholder Engagement**
  : Identify key stakeholders, analyse their expectations, and develop and execute appropriate strategies to work with them; manage and regularly engage multiple stakeholders i.e., regulators, Certification Bodies, manufacturers, assessors, technical experts, laboratories and academia to ensure timely information exchange and seamless coordination.
* **Business Development & Marketing of the Scheme**
  : Ensure quantitative improvement in the number of Certification Bodies; identify potential clients and partners for adoption of the scheme; market the scheme to increase its uptake; and develop a comprehensive plan to improve scheme processes and revenue generation.

**Eligibility Criteria & Requirements-**

**Educational Qualification**
:

* A Bachelor’s degree in Engineering in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related discipline is required. A Bachelor’s degree in a related engineering discipline, coupled with strong relevant experience, may also be considered for the Associate Manager role.
* An additional qualification in management, public policy, or conformity assessment ecosystem, or quality and compliance, or training in ISO/IEC 17065, ISO/IEC 17067, or ISO/IEC 17024, or ISO/IEC 17020, or ISO 9001 will be considered a strong added advantage.

**Experience-**

* Minimum 3 years of professional work experience in areas including manufacturing, R&D, operations, consulting (private or government), or testing, auditing or a managerial role specifically in drone industry, or should have experience with stakeholder management, or operating a certification scheme, or national program.
* Knowledge of the Drone Rules, 2021 and CSUAS is essential, along with knowledge of the relevant rules and regulations with respect to drones operations in India and type certification.
* Excellent Microsoft Office skills, strong verbal communication, and sound organisational and planning skills, with a proven ability to multitask and meet tight deadlines, are required.
* Experience in marketing of products and creation of knowledge products is desired. Prior experience of working with government agencies, regulators or CABs in any capacity (operations or consulting) will be preferred.
* Working experience in any programming language, or with dashboards and AI tools, would be an added advantage. Exposure to UAS design, manufacturing, testing or flight operations, including VLOS/BVLOS flying experience, will be preferred though not mandatory.
* Fluency in English, both written and oral, is required. Fluency in Hindi, both written and oral, is desired.
* Location for the role is based out of New Delhi, on a full time engagement, with travel anywhere in India or abroad as and when required.

**Technical Capabilities-**

**Strong Research Skills:**
Ability to rapidly identify, read, and understand dense, technical documents (e.g., government reports and research papers) and extract the most relevant information.

**Structured Thinking & Writing:**
Ability to break down large, ambiguous topics into a structured research plan and produce clear, logical, professional, and well-written outputs.

**Data Analysis:**
Comfortable with data cleaning, essential MS Excel functions, and creating charts. Experience analysing survey data using Stata, R, or Python is an added advantage.

**Visualization & Presentation Skills:**
Strong data-visualization skills using MS Office Suite, with Tableau/Power BI proficiency being an added advantage; ability to create well-structured and visually compelling presentations.

**Behavioural Capabilities-**

**High Degree of Curiosity:**
Genuine interest in how India’s public policy and governance systems work; naturally follows current affairs and asks “why.”

**Integrity & Accountability:**
Takes ownership of tasks, delivers on commitments, and upholds the highest ethical standards in all work and workplace interactions.

**Meticulous Attention to Detail:**
Able to identify typos, formatting errors, inconsistencies, and mismatched numbers that others may overlook.

**Proactive & “Get-it-Done” Attitude:**
Self-starter who takes complete ownership of tasks, anticipates what needs to be done, and delivers results without waiting for instructions.

title: Apparel (U.S. Retail Brands) – Product Integrity & Compliance Manager
description:
Apparel (U.S. Retail Brands) – Product Integrity & Compliance Manager

INDIA • REMOTE • IMMEDIATE JOINING

Working hours: U.S. Eastern business hours (6:30 PM–3:30 AM IST); corresponding India shift varies with daylight saving time.

About the role

We are seeking an experienced apparel Product Integrity & Compliance Manager to own retailer testing and product compliance coordination for major U.S. retail brands, including Costco, Walmart, Sam’s Club, and Target. This is a brand-facing, cross-functional coordination role—not a hands-on laboratory technician position. The successful candidate will communicate directly with brand, Design, Technical Design, Production, Sourcing, vendor, and third-party laboratory teams to address testing requirements, failures, corrective actions, and shipment risks.

Key responsibilities

·        Own and coordinate apparel product testing and compliance programs from product development through bulk production and shipment.

·        Communicate directly with U.S. brand-facing teams and collaborate with Design, Technical Design, Production, Sourcing, Merchandising, vendors, and factories.

·        Interpret U.S. retailer-specific testing requirements and ensure timely execution through third-party laboratories.

·        Review test reports, identify failures, coordinate root-cause investigations, corrective action plans, retesting, and product disposition recommendations.

·        Maintain testing protocols for physical, chemical, performance, and safety requirements across apparel categories.

·        Ensure adherence to relevant CPSIA, REACH, California Proposition 65, AATCC, ASTM, and ISO requirements and standards.

·        Manage children’s apparel safety reviews and retailer-specific compliance expectations.

·        Maintain accurate test records, certifications, and compliance documentation, including GRS/RCS where applicable.

·        Support vendor onboarding and training on retailer testing protocols; participate in PO handoffs, product reviews, and brand/licensor discussions.

·        Escalate testing failures, compliance risks, and shipment-impacting issues proactively to the appropriate stakeholders.

Required qualifications

·        Strong professional experience in apparel product integrity, product testing coordination, quality, or regulatory compliance.

·        Demonstrated direct communication with U.S. retail brands, buying offices, or brand-facing compliance teams—not solely forwarding reports to another laboratory.

·        Hands-on coordination with Design, Technical Design, Production, Sourcing, factories, vendors, and external laboratories.

·        Ability to interpret testing protocols and laboratory results, explain failures, and independently drive corrective actions and retesting.

·        Experience with children’s apparel product testing and safety compliance (mandatory).

·        Knowledge of CPSIA, REACH, Prop 65 and relevant AATCC, ASTM, and ISO standards.

·        Excellent spoken and written English communication; able to work independently during U.S. Eastern hours.

Preferred experience

Experience supporting testing and compliance programs for
**Costco, Walmart, Sam’s Club, Target, or comparable U.S. retailers.**

Important role distinction

**This position does not involve performing laboratory tests. Candidates whose work has been limited to bench testing or transmitting reports without direct U.S. brand-facing and cross-functional ownership are unlikely to meet the role requirements.**

What we offer

Competitive compensation and growth opportunities • Referral bonuses • Monthly team engagement activities

About the client

Our client is a leading U.S.-based apparel importer and distributor with over 40 years of experience in product design, sourcing, and end-to-end global supply chain management.

About Stride Logistics & Consultants

Stride drives efficiency across the logistics industry through technology, digital transformation, and intelligent outsourcing, helping businesses operate smarter and scale faster.

**Mandatory – Spoken Communication Assessment**

As this role requires excellent English communication skills and direct interaction with U.S. retail brands, applicants are required to submit a
**1-minute audio introduction**
highlighting their professional background, relevant apparel product integrity and compliance experience, and exposure to U.S. retail clients.

**Please share your audio introduction via WhatsApp at +91 9901613648 for preliminary screening. Please do not call this number directly, only WhatsApp. You can expect the response after 6pm.**

title: Associate - Security Governance, Risk & Compliance
description:
**Associate, Security Governance, Risk & Compliance**

**Location:**
Gurgaon, Bengaluru, Mumbai

**Experience:**
*3-5 years of relelavant exp inclusing dedicated third-party risk management experience*

**About the Company**

Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with more than 10,000 entrepreneurial, action- and results-oriented professionals across over 40 countries. A&M takes a hands-on approach to solving client problems and helping organizations reach their potential. Its culture values independent thinking, collaboration, and measurable impact, guided by Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity. Established in India in 2023, A&M Global Capability Center Private Limited partners with leadership across business units and geographies to enable efficient service delivery, specialized talent, competitive pricing, faster delivery, automation, and digital and analytics capabilities. The GCC supports end-to-end case delivery and thought leadership rather than traditional back-office work. It serves the Americas, EMEA, and APAC across industries including Consumer and Retail, Healthcare, Software and Technology, Automotive and Industrials, Hospitality and Leisure, Energy and Natural Resources, and Financial Services. The rapidly growing center already has more than 500 team members.

**About the Role**

The Security GRC Associate will own execution and improvement of the Information Security third-party risk management program. Through GRC platforms, assessment workflows, risk registers, reporting routines, and documented controls, the role will identify, evaluate, monitor, and help remediate vendor risks. The associate will complete client security questionnaires, review information security contract terms, and coordinate with Privacy, Legal, IT, procurement, and business stakeholders to produce accurate, timely responses. Success requires dedicated third-party risk management experience, including assessing at least 100 vendors annually, managing remediation within defined SLAs, and translating technical security requirements into practical business language. The role will strengthen governance visibility, support regulatory and policy compliance, and improve the firm’s ability to make risk-based decisions across vendor and client engagements.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Own vendor risk identification and assessment against A&M’s risk appetite, completing assessments for at least 100 vendors annually through approved GRC platforms and documented workflows.
* Track risk treatment, remediation commitments, security performance alerts, and overdue actions, converting current evidence into accurate monthly posture reviews and management reporting.
* Manage client security questionnaires within defined SLAs, coordinating with Privacy, Legal, IT, and business stakeholders to deliver complete, consistent, and evidence-based responses.
* Maintain and improve security assessment frameworks, questionnaires, response libraries, and supporting knowledge repositories so recurring reviews become faster, more consistent, and easier to govern.
* Evaluate information security clauses in client and vendor contracts, identifying obligations that could create exposure and aligning recommendations with security policies and compliance requirements.
* Communicate control gaps, risk ratings, and remediation strategies to technical and non-technical stakeholders, enabling proportionate decisions based on business context and risk appetite.
* Execute recurring governance activities, including metrics gathering, internal assessments, reporting, and process improvements using automation or Artificial Intelligence to increase efficiency and control visibility.

**Essential Skills & Technologies**

* Third-party risk management experience with vendor security assessments, audits, remediation tracking, GRC platforms, and annual throughput of at least 100 vendor assessments.
* Working knowledge of security controls, regulatory requirements, ISO 27001, NIST, information security questionnaires, and security terms commonly included in legal contracts.
* Strong analytical, written, verbal, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to translate technical risk into concise, business-accessible decisions and actions.

**Additional Plus**

* An industry-recognized certification such as CRISC, CTPRP, CISSP, or CISM will strengthen your ability to evaluate control maturity and advise stakeholders.
* Experience improving third-party risk processes through automation, Artificial Intelligence, workflow redesign, reporting enhancements, or structured knowledge management will be valuable.
* Exposure to global consulting, professional services, or multi-region regulatory and client environments will help you navigate varied stakeholders, obligations, and delivery expectations.

**What You'll Bring**

You will bring 4–8 years of total relevant experience, including 3–5 years dedicated to third-party risk management, governance, risk, compliance, or information security. Your background should demonstrate ownership of vendor security assessments and audits, with experience managing risk reviews for at least 100 vendors in a year. You will be comfortable using GRC and third-party risk management platforms to document findings, assign treatments, monitor remediation, and produce management reporting. You can complete client security questionnaires within agreed SLAs, maintain reliable evidence and response libraries, and collaborate with Privacy, Legal, IT, procurement, and business teams. You will understand security frameworks such as ISO 27001 and NIST, relevant regulatory expectations, security controls, and information security contract clauses. A bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Risk Management, Business, or a related field is required. CRISC, CTPRP, CISSP, or CISM certification is advantageous. You are analytical, detail-oriented, organized, and able to prioritize multiple deadlines without losing accuracy. Most importantly, you communicate risk clearly, apply sound judgment, and connect control decisions to business impact.

**Why Join Us**

* Join a rapidly growing India capability center that contributes to end-to-end global case delivery and thought leadership rather than operating as a traditional back-office function.
* Build international exposure by supporting stakeholders and clients across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC, with opportunities to solve varied third-party security and governance challenges.
* Grow in an entrepreneurial, meritocratic environment that values independent thinking, measurable impact, continuous learning, and inclusive collaboration across disciplines and geographies.

**What We Offer**

* Structured performance development, professional training, and on-the-job learning designed to build deeper expertise in security governance, third-party risk, compliance, and consulting delivery.
* Career growth opportunities within a global consulting firm and a rapidly expanding India capability center, supported by experienced leaders and cross-functional collaboration.
* A workplace that prioritizes employee well-being and provides benefits and resources supporting professional development and personal needs.
* An inclusive culture guided by Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity, with meaningful work and strong team engagement.

title: Senior Financial Crime Compliance Manager
description:
**Job Description:**
As a Senior Manager in our Financial Crime Client Delivery Services group, you will primarily be responsible for the leadership and supervision of Managers and Analysts on client projects. The successful candidate will utilize their management skills and AML/sanctions knowledge to oversee the day-to-day operations of client engagements whilst coaching and mentoring the team to meet the client's objectives. Furthermore, the role requires the individual to possess a strong entrepreneurial spirit, be highly collaborative, able to express ideas readily, manage change fluidly, and be able to influence and identify opportunities.
  
  
The Senior Manager will have direct client contact and be responsible for managing the client relationship whilst contributing to the growth of AMLRS’ business. You will also be responsible for leading meetings with clients and ensuring that client KPI/KRI and overall dashboard reporting is accurate and issued timely. Ability to identify risks and manage downward and upward communication and feedback is important.
  
  
**Primary Responsibilities**

* Lead day-to-day operations on AML/FC engagements, manage, and escalate risk accordingly
* Supervise the day-to-day operations on financial crime/AML engagements in accordance with terms of service agreements stipulated in the executed statement of work (SOW)/contract.
* Establish quality standards on the engagement and work with the Managers and/or Team Leads to ensure that an appropriate QC process is implemented to mitigate risks and adhere to client QC requirements/standards.
* Utilize AML/Financial Crime Subject Matter Expertise and judgment to prepare reports, manage, and escalate risks/issues on the engagement appropriately and timely.
* Assist the Director (or appointed lead, as applicable) on the engagement to design and implement KPI/ KRI reports.
* Identify and coordinate training needs on the project to ensure that the engagement team has the appropriate knowledge and tools to meet the client objectives.
* Attend client meetings and work with the Director (or assigned Lead, as applicable) to ensure that the appropriate AMLRS team members attend internal and external meetings.
* Work with the Manager(s) to continuously assess whether the engagement leverage model is adequate to meet engagement needs and production volumes and, at minimum, is in line with the requirements in the SOW at all times.
* Ensure that the engagement team submits their time in NetSuite correctly and on time.
* Help organize and help lead periodic touch points with client stakeholders to assess their needs and obtain feedback around AMLRS performance.
* Partner with the Director or appropriate Lead to assist in putting together appropriate materials for client monthly/quarterly/bi-annual/annual business or executive meetings with the client.
* Involvement in certain internal strategic initiatives across the Managed Services practice working closely with Directors and others.
* Mentor and coach Engagement Teams
* Promote and participate in inclusive mentoring and coaching relationships on the engagement, across all staff levels.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s Degree with 15-18 years or more of AML / Financial Crimes experience, with an understanding of regulatory requirements as it pertains to areas such as transaction monitoring, AML policies and procedures, KYC, EDD and AML independent testing.
* The following experience and/or knowledge is a plus: (i) Fraud and/or sanctions experience; (ii) Payments and/or Fintech experience; (iii) Understanding and/or knowledge of AML regulations.
* Proven ability to lead, mentor and coach teams of more than 50 employees, including Managers.
* Ability to lead projects, develop timelines, coordinate project teams and implement action items during the life of a project.
* Ability to exercise AML subject matter expertise and project management skills to effectively manage scope, budget, and timelines on AML/FC projects.
* Ability to identify and manage prompt resolution of potential risks and issues while managing client expectations.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Professional Certification
* Master’s degree
* Strong knowledge of banking industry and related regulations and laws.
* Strong entrepreneurial spirit, highly collaborative, able to express ideas readily, manage change fluidly, able to influence and identify opportunities.

AML RightSource is committed to fostering a diverse work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.
  
  
**Recruitment Scam Alerts**
**We’re aware of an increase in recruitment scams where individuals falsely claim to represent AML RightSource. These scammers may ask for money or personal information by offering fake job opportunities through e-mail, text message or social media. If you encounter suspicious messages, do not respond.**

title: Legal & Compliance Manager
description:
**Share Knowledge, Empower the World**

Arches is a global platform for expert knowledge, strategic solutions, and talent, with a particular strength in Asia. We connect people and insights to help organizations make better decisions and drive real impact. At Arches, titles don’t drive us, purpose does. We empower ambitious professionals to grow fast and work globally with the flexibility to thrive in their own way.

Since 2019, we’ve grown to become a global knowledge platform connecting 200,000+ experts across industries. With offices in 8 cities and a team of ambitious professionals from 15+ nationalities, we help the world’s top consulting firms, investors, and Fortune 500 companies make smarter decisions.

Backed by $6M+ funding and cutting-edge technology, we’re scaling faster than ever and there’s space for bold talent to grow with us.

Arches was certified as:

* **Winner of the LinkedIn Impact Awards 2026**
* **Great Place to Work® Japan 2026**
* **One of Japan’s fastest-growing companies (KUSABI Award 2025)**

Learn more about us: Arches on LinkedIn

**INDUSTRY OVERVIEW**

The
**Expert Network Services (ENS)**
industry connects our clients (consulting and investment firms) with specialized insights from top experts. With a strong focus on the Asia-Pacific region, our team is fluent in the languages ​​​​​​​​across the area and has unmatched recruitment capabilities to find experts from any industry or niche.

**ROLE OVERVIEW**

Arches is seeking a proactive and detail-oriented
**Legal Manager**
to join our global team. In the fast-paced expert network industry, navigating complex regulatory, contractual, and compliance requirements is essential to our operations.

The
**Legal Manager**
will support Arches by managing a broad portfolio of commercial contracts, monitoring regulatory developments, supporting compliance matters, and serving as a trusted advisor to internal stakeholders and clients. The ideal candidate will have experience working within an expert network firm or a related financial services, consulting, or professional services organization.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

* **Contract Lifecycle Management:**
  Draft, review, and negotiate client, vendor, and other commercial agreements, including Master Services Agreements (MSAs), Statements of Work (SOWs), Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs), Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) and related contracts.
* **Regulatory & Compliance Monitoring:**
  Monitor legal and regulatory developments relevant to the expert network industry, including data protection and privacy laws, Material Non-Public Information (MNPI) and securities laws, anti-bribery requirements, sanctions, and other cross-border regulatory matters. Recommend updates to internal documentation, policies, and processes where necessary.
* **Legal Inquiries & Disputes:**
  Assist with legal notices, disputes, regulatory inquiries, and investigations, including fact-finding, evidence gathering, and coordination with internal stakeholders and external counsel.
* **Stakeholder Communication:**
  Serve as a key point of contact for legal and compliance inquiries from internal teams and external clients. Participate in client calls and support discussions regarding compliance frameworks, contractual obligations, and risk management.
* **Operational Support:**
  Provide practical, commercially focused legal guidance to operational and business teams while helping ensure consistent service delivery and effective risk mitigation.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Law degree required (LLB, JD, or equivalent qualification); an LLM or other postgraduate law degree is preferred.
* **9-10 years of experience in a corporate or commercial legal role. Ideally, prior experience working within an expert network firm.**
* Strong experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating commercial contracts.
* Understanding of data protection and privacy laws, corporate compliance frameworks, MNPI, securities laws, and other regulatory risks relevant to expert networks.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex legal concepts clearly to legal and non-legal stakeholders.
* Strong organizational, analytical, and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a global environment.
* **Professional fluency in English.**

**PERKS AND BENEFITS**

At Arches, we believe in clear communication about your benefits, actively improving with your feedback, and providing accessible HR support.

**Here Are Some Of What To Expect:**

***Salary & Allowances***

* **Compensation & Benefits:**
* Competitive Base Salary with performance-based annual skills increases.
* 13th-month salary.
* **Paid Leave**
  – 14 days of annual leave, plus enhanced paid leave for special life milestones and financial support from Arches.
* **Insurance**
  – Private medical insurance.
* **Self-learning budget.**

***Career Growth***

* Rapid Career Advancement: Solve challenging problems for exciting startups and accelerate your career with swift promotions and a direct path to leadership.
* High-Caliber Network: Build an unparalleled network by collaborating with and learning from industry leaders at top consulting and investment firms.

***Engagement***

* Enjoy a vibrant work environment with team activities, quarterly dinners, company trips, social gatherings, and office snacks and drinks. Support for employee well-being also includes sports clubs (badminton, golf, football, etc.).
* **Flexible Work Arrangements**

description:
**Selected Intern's Day-to-day Responsibilities Include**
Contract Management-Draft, review, negotiate, and finalize commercial agreements, including vendor agreements, service agreements, NDAs, licensing agreements, manufacturing agreements, and other business contracts.
  
  
Identify legal risks and provide practical recommendations to mitigate such risks.
  
  
Maintain and manage contract repositories and track contractual obligations.
  
  
Legal Advisory-Provide legal advice and support to various business functions on day-to-day operational matters.
  
  
Assist in structuring transactions and evaluating legal implications of business decisions.
  
  
Interpret laws, regulations, and contractual provisions for internal stakeholders.
  
  
Compliance & Regulatory-Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and internal policies.
  
  
Support implementation and monitoring of compliance programs.
  
  
Coordinate with external counsel and regulatory authorities as required.
  
  
Litigation & Dispute Management-Assist in handling litigation, arbitration, consumer complaints, and regulatory proceedings.
  
  
Coordinate with external lawyers on ongoing cases.
  
  
Review legal notices and prepare responses.
  
  
Intellectual Property- Assist in the protection and management of trademarks, copyrights, and other intellectual property assets.
  
  
Coordinate filing, renewal, and enforcement activities with external IP counsel.
  
  
Corporate Secretarial Support- Support corporate governance and statutory compliance activities.
  
  
Assist in maintaining legal and corporate records.

title: Senior Manager QPPV Office
description:
Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today!
  
  
**Job Details**
**Job Responsibilities**
The Senior Manager, Pharmacovigilance Agreements (PVA) is a key member of the QPPV Office (QPPVO) organization and serves as the functional lead for the management and governance of Pharmacovigilance Agreements (PVAs) across a diverse portfolio of clients, partnerships, and pharmacovigilance systems.
  
  

* The role combines strategic oversight with hands-on operational responsibility, ensuring that pharmacovigilance contractual obligations are accurately defined, effectively implemented, and maintained in compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and industry expectations.
* The incumbent is responsible for the end-to-end lifecycle management of PVAs, including agreement planning, authoring, review, negotiation support, implementation, maintenance, reconciliation, and periodic review.
* This includes direct involvement in drafting and updating agreements, coordinating stakeholder reviews, tracking implementation activities, managing agreement repositories, ensuring timely execution of contractual updates, and supporting the translation of contractual obligations into operational pharmacovigilance processes.
* Acting as the primary subject matter expert for PVA-related activities, the Senior Manager provides guidance on the allocation of pharmacovigilance responsibilities between business partners and ensures consistency across PVAs, Quality Agreements, contractual documentation, PSMFs, procedural documents, and operational practices.
* The role supports client-facing discussions, due diligence activities, business development initiatives, partnership transitions, and regulatory inspections by providing expert contractual and compliance oversight.
* Close collaboration with QPPVs, Local Safety Officers, Pharmacovigilance Operations, Medical Information, Regulatory Affairs, Quality Assurance, Legal, Commercial, Business Development, Project Management, and external client stakeholders.
* Proactively identify contractual compliance risks, resolve gaps and ambiguities, support CAPA implementation, and contribute to inspection readiness initiatives.
* As an integral member of the QPPV Office, the role is not limited to PVA management activities. Depending on business priorities, resource requirements, and organizational needs, the Senior Manager may also be required to support broader QPPVO governance activities, including PSMF management and maintenance, inspection and audit readiness, compliance monitoring, quality management initiatives, procedural development, governance reporting, onboarding and training programs, and other operational or strategic projects within the QPPV Office.
* The incumbent is therefore expected to maintain a broad understanding of pharmacovigilance system governance and contribute flexibly to the overall objectives and success of the QPPVO function.

**Qualification**
Bachelor's degree in life sciences, pharmacy, medicine, nursing, public health, epidemiology, regulatory affairs, or a related field, or equivalent experience required.

4+ years of experience in pharmacovigilance, drug safety, epidemiology, risk management, scientific consulting, regulatory affairs, or a related field required.

description:
**Company Description**
My Visa Source Legal – US & Canada Immigration Lawyers is an award-winning, full-service immigration law firm with an experienced team of Canadian lawyers and licensed practitioners. The firm provides legal solutions for personal and business immigration matters across Canada and the United States, with physical offices in Toronto, Vancouver and Scottsdale, Arizona. Its mission is to offer clear, effective legal guidance that improves the likelihood of favorable outcomes for clients from diverse backgrounds. My Visa Source uses efficient, proven processes and up-to-date knowledge of immigration laws and trends, contributing to its status as one of North America’s fastest-growing immigration law firms. The firm has received multiple national and international awards recognizing excellence in corporate and personal immigration services.

**Role Description The Immigration Case Analyst is a full-time remote role responsible for supporting the preparation, organization, and tracking of immigration files for both personal and business clients. This role involves gathering and reviewing client documents, performing legal and policy research, summarizing case facts, and drafting clear, accurate case notes and supporting materials under lawyer supervision. The analyst will communicate with clients to clarify information, follow up on outstanding documentation, and ensure timelines and filing deadlines are met. Day-to-day tasks include coordinating with legal team members, updating case management systems, maintaining accurate records, and helping streamline workflows to improve efficiency and client experience. The role requires a high level of attention to detail, discretion with sensitive information, and a commitment to service excellence in a fast-paced, deadline-driven env

ironment.
**Qualifications**

* Strong analytical and research abilities, including the capacity to interpret immigration regulations, policies, and official guidance, and summarize findings clearly.
* Excellent written communication skills for drafting case summaries, correspondence, and supporting documents, with strong grammar, clarity, and precision.
* High level of organization and time management skills to handle multiple files, manage deadlines, and maintain accurate digital records in case management systems.
* Client service and interpersonal skills, including the ability to communicate respectfully and clearly with clients from diverse backgrounds and maintain confidentiality.
* Technical proficiency with common office software (e.g., document editors, spreadsheets, PDF tools) and comfort learning new legal or CRM platforms.
* Post-secondary education in law, paralegal studies, political science, international relations, or a related field; paralegal or legal assistant training is an asset.
* Prior experience in immigration law, legal services, or a regulated professional environment is preferred but not mandatory.
* Ability to work independently in a remote setting, collaborate effectively with a distributed team, and adapt to evolving processes and priorities.
* Strong ethical judgment, attention to detail, and commitment to accuracy when dealing with sensitive personal and corporate information.**

title: Functional Head – Corporate Affairs & Legal
description:
**Job Purpose**

* Functional Head – Corporate Affairs & Legal will provide strategic and functional leadership across Corporate Affairs and Legal, ensuring compliance with applicable laws and regulations, effective Board and stakeholder management, legal risk mitigation, and successful execution of M&A activities. The role will also ensure adherence to management policies and procedures, including applicable technical, environmental and occupational health and safety standards.

Company Background
  
  

* A leading automotive tier 1 company

Key Responsibilities
  
  
Corporate Affairs Strategy
  
  

* Develop and implement the long-term strategy for the Corporate Affairs function in alignment with company’s business objectives and growth plans.
* Establish effective processes and controls to strengthen governance, compliance and risk management across the organisation.
* Advise senior management on corporate affairs matters, legal implications and regulatory developments that may impact business operations.
* Company Secretarial & Corporate Governance
* Oversee all company secretarial activities, ensuring timely and accurate statutory filings, disclosures, Annual General Meetings (AGMs) and other regulatory obligations.
* Manage Board and Committee proceedings, including preparation of agendas, minutes, resolutions, statutory records and required disclosures.
* Ensure compliance with applicable corporate laws and governance requirements, maintaining transparency, accountability and regulatory discipline.

Legal Affairs & Risk Management
  
  

* Oversee legal matters, litigation, notices and disputes in coordination with empanelled lawyers and external legal counsel.
* Review, vet and validate commercial contracts, agreements, joint venture arrangements and technical assistance agreements to protect the organisation’s interests.
* Identify potential legal and contractual risks, assess their implications and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.
* Coordinate with internal departments and external counsel to ensure timely resolution of legal matters.

Regulatory Affairs & Government Relations
  
  

* Develop and maintain effective relationships with government authorities and regulatory bodies.
* Coordinate with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), Registrar of Companies (ROC) and other relevant authorities to ensure compliance with applicable requirements.
* Oversee regulatory approvals, statutory submissions and related interactions, ensuring timely resolution of regulatory matters.
* Investor Relations & Stakeholder Management
* Oversee investor relations activities, particularly those related to corporate governance, disclosures and transactions.
* Maintain effective engagement with the Board, joint venture partners, auditors, banking partners, legal advisors and other key stakeholders.
* Facilitate coordination between internal functions and external stakeholders on matters requiring legal, regulatory or corporate governance inputs.

Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A)
  
  

* Lead the end-to-end M&A lifecycle, including opportunity evaluation, valuation, due diligence, transaction structuring and execution.
* Coordinate with financial advisors, legal counsel, banking partners and other third parties involved in transactions.
* Oversee pre- and post-transaction governance, ensuring appropriate controls, documentation and compliance throughout the transaction lifecycle.
* Work with senior management to evaluate transaction-related risks and support informed decision-making.

Functional / Technical Skills
  
  

* Corporate & Company Law: Strong understanding of the Companies Act, company secretarial practices and applicable Indian statutes.
* Corporate Governance: Expertise in Board and Committee management, statutory filings, regulatory disclosures and governance processes.
* Legal & Contract Management: Ability to assess contractual terms, manage litigation, evaluate legal risks and coordinate with external legal counsel.
* Regulatory Compliance: Understanding of statutory requirements and regulatory interactions relevant to the organisation.
* M&A and Transaction Management: Exposure to valuation, due diligence, transaction structuring, legal documentation and post-transaction governance.
* Financial Acumen: Ability to interpret financial information and apply financial analytics to support transaction evaluation and business decisions.
* Risk Assessment: Ability to identify legal, regulatory and contractual risks and develop appropriate mitigation strategies.

Key Interactions
  
  

* Internal Stakeholders: Chairperson and Managing Director, Executive Directors, Central Department Heads & Plant Heads
* External Stakeholders: Board or JV Partners, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Registrar of Companies, Legal experts (Empanelled Lawyers)

Qualification and Professional Experience
  
  

* Qualification: ICAI or ICSI (Company Secretary) qualification is required. An LLB and MBA are desirable.
* Overall Experience: 18–20 years of relevant industry experience.
* Leadership Experience: More than three years of experience in a similar leadership role.
* Functional Expertise: Strong experience in Corporate Affairs, Company Secretarial matters, Legal Management, Corporate Governance and Statutory Compliance.
* M&A Exposure: Experience in mergers and acquisitions, including valuation, due diligence, transaction structuring and post-transaction governance.
* Stakeholder Management: Experience in managing external legal counsel, regulatory authorities and senior-level stakeholders.
* Team Leadership: Proven ability to lead teams, manage competing priorities and ensure effective execution of functional responsibilities.

title: Lead - Regulatory
description:
**Lead – Regulatory Affairrs**
At ENGIE, we are accelerating the energy transition across the globe. Our teams shape the policies, partnerships, and strategies that drive clean energy forward. We need people who see the bigger picture and act on it.
  
  
In this role, you will be at the intersection of regulation, policy, and business growth. You will influence outcomes that matter — for ENGIE, for the industry, and for a sustainable future. If you thrive on navigating complex regulatory landscapes and building strategic relationships, this is your opportunity.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Provide insights on industry and market developments, including policy and regulatory updates, to advocate for favourable outcomes.
* Analyse regulations, guidelines, policies, and government orders to deliver actionable recommendations to senior leadership.
* Support policy advocacy efforts by drafting and filing petitions with appropriate regulatory and legal authorities.

* Draft Memorandums of Understanding with government bodies, aligning them with legal and strategic frameworks.

* Proven ability to engage with government bodies, regulators, and industry associations at senior levels.
* Excellent analytical skills with the ability to translate complex regulations into clear, strategic recommendations.
* Outstanding written and verbal communication skills for drafting representations, petitions, and stakeholder communications.
* A degree in Law, Public Policy, Engineering, or a related field; an advanced degree is preferred.
* A collaborative mindset with the ability to work across functions including legal, business development, and project teams.

* A career path with real growth opportunities within a global energy leader operating in over 30 countries.
* A diversity of missions spanning regulatory strategy, policy advocacy, stakeholder engagement, and business development.
* Stimulating work that directly shapes the energy transition in one of the world's fastest-growing markets.
* A friendly and collaborative work environment where your voice is heard and your contributions are valued.

At ENGIE, every talent has a role to play in accelerating the energy transition. Make a difference and enjoy a fulfilling professional experience. Take on exciting challenges and build a career path that reflects who you are. Join us and be part of the adventure of the century!

description:
Law House of Lily Thomas & Saju Jakob (Advocates & Solicitors): It is a law firm rooted in a legacy of late Adv. Lily Thomas (Lily Thomas vs Union of India). This law office stands for humanity, social justice, and constitutional values. Inspired by the work and teachings of our senior and mentor Lily Thomas, this law house focuses on protecting individual rights and advancing constitutional morality. The practice spans multiple areas including constitutional law, service law, family law, civil law, criminal law, banking law, and taxation law, with strong representation before the Supreme Court, High Courts, and Trial Courts. The firm is known for providing practical, clear, and timely legal solutions to its clients. In addition to legal practice, the firm engages in academic and social initiatives through memorial lectures and essay competitions.

**Role Description- Long Term Paid Internship ( 4 to 6 Months)**
–
will work on legal research, drafting, and analysis related to cross-border legal issues and matters involving foreign elements, under the supervision of senior lawyers.

• Public and private international law

• Constitutional and comparative constitutional law

• International family law - Divorce, Child Custody, and other related issues,

• Domestic and international arbitration

• International taxation law- Avoidance of Double Taxation

• Domestic and international legal issues

. Private International Law - Internaitonal Contracts

The role involves coordinating with teams handling constitutional, civil, criminal, banking, and taxation matters where private international law issues arise. The position is a full-time, on-site role based in New Delhi, requiring regular collaboration with colleagues, participation in client meetings, and contribution to the firm’s knowledge-building activities.

* Candidates should possess a strong foundation in
  **Law**

  **Legal Document Preparation**

* Candidates should possess strong
  **Analytical Skills**
  for interpreting statutes, case law, and international instruments, and for developing reasoned legal arguments.
* Candidates should possess effective
  **Communication**
  abilities, including clear written and verbal communication with courts, colleagues, and clients.
* Candidates should possess the ability to identify, assess, and address complex
  **Legal Issues**
  across multiple practice areas. Students pursuing an LL.B. or LL.M. who can commit to an internship of at least six months.
* Applicants who have written articles or research papers, or have undertaken research in any of these areas, are especially encouraged to apply.
* Attention to detail, professionalism, ethical integrity, and the ability to work in a collaborative, on-site environment in New Delhi.

Interested candidates may send their CV and a brief note describing their research or writing experience by LinkedIn message. Please include your

title: Legal & Compliance Manager - Wealth
description:
**Legal & Compliance Lead ( IC role)**

**SBNRI · Gurgaon · Reports to the CEO**

**About SBNRI**

35 million NRIs are trying to manage money in India from thousands of miles away. Most of them don't trust anyone enough to help. SBNRI is building the company that changes that, across mutual funds, fixed deposits, taxation, and cross-border compliance, for investors in over 120 countries.

Our users live under one country's rules and invest under another's. Regulation isn't a constraint on this business. It is the business.

**What you'll own**

See risk early. Track SEBI, AMFI, RBI, IFSCA and FIU-IND, along with industry and global regulatory reports. Spot changes about six months before they land. Assess whether SBNRI can absorb each change, what it costs our growth, and what we need to do now to be ready.

**Say yes, safely**
. Assess new products, partnerships and markets for feasibility. Answer three questions: what is allowed, what approvals we need, and how to structure it so it works.

**Keep the line clear**

.
Keep distribution and advice separate across our products, marketing and customer conversations. Review campaigns quickly enough that growth never waits on you.

**Run the machine**
. Own the compliance calendar, obligations register, KYC/AML framework, data protection, audits, regulator queries and grievances. Turn every recurring check into a system others can run.

**Handle the paperwork that matters.**
Review agreements with AMCs, banks, partners and vendors. Work with external counsel when a question needs specialist depth. Report to the Board on compliance risk and remediation.

**Our non-negotiables**

A path, not a verdict.
**"Not permitted"**
is half an answer. Say what would be permitted instead. If the answer is no, say so early.

**Fast and right.**
Give a same-day view on reversible questions. Give a written recommendation on irreversible ones.

**No surprises.**
No regulatory change or deadline should reach us late. Missing one means the system you own has failed.

**Inspection-proof**
. Send nothing to a user or a regulator that you would not defend on record.

Systems over dependency. If you are doing something by hand for the third time, automate it or turn it into a checklist.

**Who we're looking for**

**6–7 years in compliance at a wealthtech, mutual fund distributor, sub-broker, broker or AMC**
. You have handled real AMFI and SEBI issues yourself, not just read about them.

**Deep SEBI and AMFI knowledge of MF distribution**
: NRI onboarding, KYC/KRA, FATCA/CRS, distributor vs adviser obligations, and commission disclosures.

**Strong grounding in corporate and business law**
. A law degree or CS qualification is a plus but not required.

Working knowledge of
**FEMA and NRI rules,**
or the drive to learn them fast. This covers NRE/NRO/FCNR accounts, repatriation and OCI rules.

**A wide view of the industry.**
You know how peers at other AMCs, distributors and fintechs have handled similar problems. You follow national and global regulatory reports.

A problem solver who likes learning. IFSCA/GIFT City,
**AML/PMLA, DPDP**
and foreign marketing rules will be new territory in parts. We will back you with specialists.

**What we offer**

A direct line to the founders and a seat in product and business decisions

A budget for external counsel, including foreign local counsel

Modern AI tools for research and drafting

A path to Head of Legal & Compliance as we scale

**This is not for you if**

You want to be the reviewer at the end of a process

You wait for someone else to resolve an unclear question.

You need a large team to be effective.

title: Contract Manager
description:
**The Opportunity**
You as a Contract Manager, will be part of Power Grids, Grid Integration (PGGI) business based in Hitachi Energy (HE)Office, Gurgaon, India. With analytical, hands-on and autonomous approach, you contribute to the successful performance of contract through your Contract Management skill in the assigned project. You shall be a reliable partner, when it comes to the day-to-day contract administration and project execution, flow-down and preparation of subcontracts/purchase orders. You will be required to ensure that contract management, change management and risk management activities are timely and accurately executed protecting HE’s interests throughout project(s) lifecycle.
  
  
**How You’ll Make An Impact**

* Ensuring that own assigned portfolio of contracts or specific project(s) (back-office or at the site) follow contract and claim management methodologies in accordance with applicable procedures.
* Provides guidance and leadership on contract related matters to cross-functional project team members.
* Developing contract management strategy based on HE’s policies, customer requirements, and the overall execution strategy considering risk, pricing, scope, and schedule.
* Identifying the contract baseline (including terms and conditions, specifications, drawings, estimate, proposal, schedule and other documents incorporated in the contract) and highlighting areas of opportunities and potential risk.
* Ensuring timely and accurate execution of commercial aspects in portfolio of contracts / subcontracts (e.g., payments, claims, variation orders, warranties, provisions, guarantees, etc.).
* Verifying that all parties to the contract have fulfilled their contractual obligations and there are no responsibilities outstanding.
* Assessing the success of the contract and determines if there are any lessons learned for future contracting.
* Documenting and communicating to all relevant parties any deficiencies found as part of the closeout process.
* Establishing and enforcing standard methodologies in portfolio of contracts to identify, notify, enforce or defend changes / claims (passive/active) coming from / towards third parties.
* In concert with HE Legal, develops the negotiation strategy and supports negotiations. Supports HE Legal in handling dispute resolution, litigation and arbitration proceedings. Notifies and liaises with HE Legal to report major claims and keeps HE Legal updated on any critical development during project execution.
* Supporting in drafting of contracts, subcontracts and supply contracts and ensuring that relevant (supply / sub) contracts contain appropriate contract terms to protect HE's interest including flow-down of main contract terms.
* Analyzing contract terms to highlight areas of potential opportunity and risk.
* Seeking advice from HE Legal to draft, negotiating and finalizing agreements during the Project execution phases.
* Developing and implementing risk mitigation and opportunity plans in collaboration with relevant stakeholders.
* Ensures insurance provisions within the contract are adhered to and coordinates with Insurance Risk Management regarding occurrences that may be covered by customer / third party or HE provided insurance. Supporting Insurance Risk Management in producing damage reports.
* Seeking advice from HE Legal/Export Control to ensure accurate handling of all export control matters regarding restrictions on exports, applicable destination laws considering countries, customers or products involved and the respective laws and HE regulations.
* Ensuring that the information and data are protected as per HE’s policies and relevant NDA/confidentiality agreements are in place while sharing of information with other parties.
* Responsible to ensure compliance with applicable external and internal regulations, procedures, and guidelines.
* Living Hitachi Energy’s core values of safety and integrity, which means taking responsibility for your own actions while caring for your colleagues and the business.

**Your background**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quantity Surveying, Business Administration, Economics or Law.
* Working knowledge and hands-on experience on contracts executed under common law/Indian law.
* Preferably 10 years or more hands-on experience in EPC projects within the fields of power generation, substations, converter stations, grid integration, transmission or similar industrial plant within a Contract Management and Subcontract Management functions (with emphasis on civil and electrical installations interfaces).
* Demonstrating successful experience in processing, managing and administrating varying sizes, types and complexity of contractual agreements during the execution and closing stages of projects lifecycle.
* Previous experience in the Indian power transmission/grid projects is highly desirable.
* Solid experience in project’s change management, claim management and contract-related legal issues and the possible effects in the relevant areas of responsibility regarding proposal stage and/or project execution.
* Ability to interface and negotiate with customers and subcontractors regarding all matters related to contracts and projects including those related to the review and process of changes.
* Ability to work in a corporate office and/or project site environment
* Proficiency in both spoken & written English language is required.

**Job Summary**
PFI Innovation Centre India is an exciting new innovation center. We’re building a future that helps people live better lives longer— and we’re looking for bold thinkers and team players to help us do it.
  
  
Here, you'll tackle complex challenges, collaborate with brilliant minds across the globe, and grow your career while helping millions achieve financial security.

While the PFI brand is new to India, you’ll be a part of the Prudential Financial, Inc. family. Founded in 1875 in Newark, New Jersey, we serve 50 million customers across more than 50 countries. With $1.334 trillion in assets, we're a global leader in institutional asset management. The 2nd largest life insurer in the US and the 9th largest institutional global asset manager.
  
  
At PFI Innovation Centre India, you’ll find a high-performance culture that’s flexible, collaborative and grounded in respect. We engage with candor, take calibrated risks, and hold ourselves accountable — always focused on delivering for our customers. It’s the standard we choose every day as we grow, perform, and win as one team.
  
  
We offer valuable leadership, mentoring and learning opportunities, paired with the flexibility and support to help you thrive.
  
  
Whether you're just starting out or ready to take your next step, we’ll help you grow with purpose and do the best work of your career.
  
  
The Associate, GSP, Third-Party Risk Management will support the Specialist and Manager across two primary functional areas: (1) Policy Documentation & Governance and (2) Monitoring & Analytics. This role helps ensure accuracy, transparency, and compliance with Global Sourcing & Procurement (GSP) policies, standards, and standard operating procedures across the company’s global operations.
  
  
The Associate will assist in drafting and maintaining documentation, conducting monitoring activities, compiling analytics, and preparing reporting used by leadership and risk committees. This role supports the company’s global governance model for sourcing, onboarding, assessing, contracting, managing, and terminating vendor relationships.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
***Policy Documentation & Governance Responsibilities***

* Assist in drafting, editing, and formatting GSP policies, standards, and SOPs.
* Maintain document libraries, templates, and version control.
* Ensure documentation reflects regulatory, audit, and business-driven updates.
* Support the tracking of policy publication workflows.
* Help prepare communication and training materials.
* Collaborate with Procurement, TPRM, Legal, Compliance, and Operational Risk teams to gather and verify requirements.

**Monitoring & Analytics Responsibilities**

* Execute monitoring and compliance testing following documented procedures.
* Record testing results accurately and ensure proper evidence retention.
* Compile data for dashboards, trackers, and scorecards.
* Support identification of trends and potential control weaknesses.
* Assist in preparing executive ready reports and presentations.
* Help track remediation activities with stakeholders.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree required.
* 0–2 years of experience in Procurement, Risk & Controls, Compliance, Audit, Data Analytics, or related fields.
* Strong written communication skills with attention to clarity and accuracy.
* Basic analytical skills with ability to interpret data.
* Ability to collaborate in a global, matrixed environment.
* Strong organization, follow through, and attention to detail.
* Proficiency in Excel or basic reporting tools preferred.
* Familiarity with documentation or workflow tools (e.g., SharePoint, Confluence) preferred.
* Fluent in AI-enabled environments, using approved tools responsibly to improve throughput, accuracy, and insight while adhering to the company’s risk and governance standards. At a minimum, all GSP employees should be able to leverage AI tools to draft, extract, validate, and optimize content that is applicable to their respective function and utilize AI tools to consistently create new content, innovation, and idea generation.

**Skills And Competencies**

* Ensure accuracy and precision in documentation
* Apply analytical thinking to identify issues and trends
* Demonstrate strong risk and control awareness
* Deliver high quality reporting support
* Collaborate effectively across teams
* Communicate clearly and concisely
* Exhibit accountability and ownership
* Demonstrate curiosity and willingness to learn

**Work Environment**

* Hybrid in Gurgaon, India

title: Software Licence Compliance Intelligence Manager
description:
**Role overview**

We are seeking a highly analytical, commercially minded and results-driven
**Software Licence Compliance Intelligence Manager**
to join our Global Licence Compliance team.

This role is suited to a data analyst with a strong understanding of software licence compliance and the ability to turn intelligence into well-founded investigative and commercial decisions. The successful candidate will analyse data gathered through software intelligence and monitoring tools—including platforms such as Revenera and Cylynt—to identify, assess and prioritise potential non-compliance and infringement opportunities.

The role requires more than producing analysis or reports. The analyst will assess the reliability and significance of available information, use sound judgement to determine appropriate next steps, and identify opportunities that can support business development and market expansion. This includes working with relevant stakeholders to decide which leads warrant further investigation, escalation or commercial follow-up.

The successful candidate will play a central role in managing and interpreting software piracy data collected through our monitoring technologies, identifying potential copyright infringements and transforming technical information into actionable Licence Compliance opportunities.

Our mission is to reduce non-compliant software use by proactively addressing infringements while fostering constructive engagement with businesses to create opportunities for the future.

**Key responsibilities**

***Data Analysis & Intelligence***

* Manage, process, analyse and interpret large volumes of software usage and piracy-related data collected through different monitoring technologies.
* Perform data cleaning, processing, and validation to improve investigation accuracy
* Use and interpret intelligence gathered through software monitoring and compliance tools, including Revenera and Cylynt, or comparable platforms.
* Conduct OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence) research to gather evidence on infringement cases.
* Maintain accurate records of investigations and compliance cases.
* Use data visualisation and business intelligence tools to identify trends, monitor performance and communicate findings.
