title: Litigation Manager (4-5 years)
description:
**Position Overview**

Delhivery is looking for a law graduate with 4–5 years of relevant litigation experience to join its Litigation team in Gurugram. The role involves independently managing litigation filed by or against Delhivery across India — commercial, recovery, labour, consumer, civil and criminal matters — including reviewing notices received, drafting and vetting replies, notices, written statements and evidence, and formulating and recommending strategy on the way forward for current and existing matters. The candidate will monitor all pending litigation; coordinate with internal business and ground teams to gather evidence and inputs for replies, notices, written statements and other court/tribunal filings; and manage and coordinate with external counsel, including assigning new matters and overseeing how they are handled. The ideal candidate will have sharp legal acumen and the ability to strategise, and will be resourceful, organised and people-oriented, with strong follow-up skills and the ability to manage cases independently with minimal supervision.

**Key Responsibilities**

***1. Litigation Management & Drafting***

• Independently manage and respond to commercial, recovery, labour, consumer, civil and criminal matters across India; review notices received and draft, vet and finalize replies, notices, written statements, pleadings and evidence before filing.

• Take the call on assigning matters to external counsel, driving litigation strategy, filings and hearings, and proactively flag risks and escalations to management.

• Track litigation timelines, monitor court proceedings, maintain accurate, up-to-date trackers and ensure timely resolution of issues such as AR attendance, document filing and orders with external counsel.

***2. Evidence & Internal Coordination***

• Coordinate with internal departments (HR, Security, Finance, Revenue Assurance) and business/ground teams to obtain accurate data and factual inputs; manage, protect and collate evidence for use in replies and pleadings.

• Draft responses independently or route them to counsel, and review counsel's drafts for accuracy and alignment with the company's position before filing.

• Act as the primary liaison between the Litigation team, internal stakeholders and external counsel; drive timely documentation, appearances and compliance across functions.

***3. Counsel & Court Coordination***

• Coordinate with external counsel for hearings, filings, conferences and documentation, representing the Litigation team's interests throughout.

• Facilitate execution of affidavits, vakalatnamas and authorisations, and coordinate attendance of company representatives and witnesses before courts and authorities, ensuring adequate preparation.

***4. Strategy, Team & Operations***

• Strategise and advise business teams on legal escalations and potential litigation, recommending a course of action based on risk assessment; identify recurring issues and recommend process or policy changes.

• Own day-to-day litigation operations, calendars, document repositories, litigation reports, counsel invoices and court-fee approvals and drive improvements in tracking and document management.

**Qualifications & Experience**

• LL.B. from a recognised university or institution.

• 4–5 years of relevant litigation or litigation-management experience (in-house or law firm) across commercial, recovery, labour, consumer, civil or criminal matters.

• Demonstrated experience independently managing litigation end-to-end, with minimal supervision.

• Familiarity with court procedures, particularly in Delhi/NCR.

• Proven experience coordinating with external counsel and internal stakeholders on case strategy.

• Ability to independently navigate court and tribunal websites.

Bar Council enrolment preferred.

**Key Skills & Attributes**

• Sharp legal acumen with strong drafting and reviewing skills across notices, pleadings and evidence.

• Resourceful, proactive and solution-oriented, with the confidence to own matters and a small team independently.

• Strong analytical ability and sound judgment in assessing litigation risk and strategy.

• Excellent follow-up skills and the ability to drive closure of action items across stakeholders.

• Clear, confident communication skills, both written and verbal.

• High level of organization, attention to detail and ownership.

• Ability to manage multiple matters, a small team and competing priorities under pressure.

Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and litigation trackers; high integrity and professionalism.

title: Company Secretary
description:
You will serve as the Company Secretary for SATL and GTCI, ensuring strong corporate governance, regulatory compliance, board management, statutory filings, investor relations, and secretarial operations for a listed entity and group companies in India.
  
  
**Job Summary**
As the Company Secretary for Goodyear South Asia Tyres Private Limited and Goodyear Technology Centre India Private Limited, you will support the end-to-end corporate governance, regulatory compliance, and secretarial functions for a listed entity and two group companies in India. You will partner with leadership, legal, finance, and external stakeholders to ensure compliance with the Companies Act, 2013, SEBI regulations, stock exchange requirements, and best-in-class governance standards.
  
  

* Corporate Governance & Compliance
* You will ensure compliance with the Companies Act, 2013, SEBI (LODR) Regulations, and other applicable statutory requirements for a listed company and two group companies in India.
* You will support the implementation and monitoring of corporate governance frameworks, policies, and compliance practices.
* You will track regulatory changes and advise relevant stakeholders on compliance implications.
* You will demonstrate strong knowledge of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, Related Party Transactions, Dividend regulations, Insider Trading regulations, Takeover Code, Materiality requirements, and other applicable regulatory provisions.
* Board, Committee & General Meetings
* You will support the planning, coordination, and execution of Board Meetings, Committee Meetings, and Annual General Meetings.
* You will prepare and circulate agendas, board packs, notices, resolutions, and supporting documentation.
* You will draft, finalize, and maintain minutes and records in accordance with statutory and regulatory requirements.
* Statutory Filings & Regulatory Reporting
* You will ensure timely filings with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), SEBI, and Stock Exchanges.
* You will prepare and submit periodic disclosures, quarterly and annual filings, annual returns, and other regulatory reports within prescribed timelines.
* Secretarial Documentation & Records
* You will maintain statutory registers, records, and corporate documentation as required under the Companies Act and SEBI regulations.
* You will support the preparation of AGM Notices, newspaper publications, annual reports, and other statutory communications.
* Investor Relations & Shareholder Services
* You will manage shareholder communications and coordinate with the Registrar & Transfer Agent (RTA).
* You will respond to investor queries and shareholder grievances in a timely and effective manner.
* You will support dividend-related activities, including declaration processes, payments, and unpaid dividend management.
* Postal Ballot & IEPF Compliance
* You will manage the end-to-end postal ballot process and related secretarial compliances.
* You will ensure compliance with Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) requirements, including transfer of shares, unclaimed dividends, and related filings.
* Insider Trading & Internal Compliance Systems
* You will manage and monitor internal compliance tools and Code of Conduct systems.
* You will ensure compliance with the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations and maintain all related records and disclosures.
* Cross-Functional Coordination
* You will work closely with legal, finance, and other internal teams to ensure alignment on compliance and governance matters.
* You will support the implementation of compliance calendars, governance processes, and internal control mechanisms

**Experience**

* You should be a qualified Company Secretary (CS) with 8+ years of post-qualification experience in corporate secretarial, governance, compliance, and regulatory affairs functions.
* You have hands-on experience working in a listed company environment, with strong exposure to the Companies Act, 2013, SEBI (LODR) Regulations, SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, Related Party Transactions, Takeover Code, and corporate governance requirements.

is the single-family office of the C.P. Gurnani family and operates as a sub-entity within the family operating business,
**Assago Group.**

The family office manages capital across public markets, private companies and external managers,

alongside the family's wider financial and administrative affairs, including cross-border structures, group companies, real estate, trusts and succession planning.

**The Role**

This role
**anchors the service and compliance function of the family office**
—
**family-office operations, cross-border compliance, banking, tax, portfolio administration, entity governance and family engagement.**
This is not a conventional back-office role. It involves cross-border filings, entity administration, portfolio data integrity, and the working relationships with the banks, advisors and fund managers the office depends on.

The role requires someone
**who can take ownership without constant supervision, understand when to act independently and when to escalate, and bring structure to complex financial and administrative matters.**

The successful candidate will become a key operating partner to the family and will provide functional oversight and coordination across the family-office operations team.

Family-office experience is preferred but not essential. Strong candidates from private banking service and compliance, Big Four compliance or tax, or similar multi-entity financial operations roles will also be considered.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Banking, Onboarding and Asset Consolidation**

* Run KYC and re-KYC cycles across all entities and family members, in India and offshore.
* Manage digital onboarding onto new investment platforms and funds; map and consolidate assets across banking relationships.
* Handle fund drawdowns, capital calls and distributions — tracking notices, arranging payment and confirming credit.

**Portfolio Data & Reporting**

* Own the family office reporting platform — historical data migration, position tagging and valuation reconciliation across custodians.
* Collect and reconcile monthly statements across roughly a dozen institutions — private banks, wealth platforms, PMS managers and AIFs.
* Prepare consolidated cross-asset portfolio reviews and strategic insight summaries for family decision-making.

**Tax, Trust & Succession**

* Coordinate ITR filings and entity financials with the family CA.
* Manage advance tax, trust administration and reporting cycles with the offshore trustee and administrator.
* Support domestic and overseas trust and will formation for succession planning.
* Assemble cost-basis and transaction history across two decades of holdings.

**Stakeholder Management**

The role coordinates a wide external network — private bankers, custodians, wealth advisors, execution partners, Big Four advisors, the family CA, offshore corporate secretaries, fund managers and trustees. Keeping these parties aligned and to timetable is a
**substantial and continuous part of the work.**

**Cross-Border Transactions & Compliance**

* Manage reporting and compliance for the family's
  **offshore investments**
  , drawing on a working knowledge of overseas investment regulations.
* Administer the
  **Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS)**
  across family members — tracking utilisation against annual limits per individual, preparing Form A2 and supporting declarations, coordinating remittances with the authorised dealer bank, and maintaining the audit trail for overseas investments and offshore accounts.
* Manage
  **offshore entity compliance**
  for the group structures — annual returns and AGMs, IRAS tax filings, statutory records, and coordination with the corporate secretary and tax agents.
* Liaise with the
  **auditors**
  and external advisors to ensure compliance with all applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.
* Lead LLP formations and administration for new investment vehicles, including ROC filings and related secretarial work.

**Real Estate and Group Companies**

* Oversee property documentation, mutation processes and developer payment schedules.
* Support group company matters including share certificates, board records and transaction
* documentation.

**Family Engagement**

* Serve as a
  **trusted operational point of contact for family members**
  on financial, administrative and investment-related matters.
* Communicate clearly and proactively, particularly where multiple advisors or institutions are involved.
* Maintain at least one in-person meeting or interaction each month with senior family members.

**What We Are Looking For**

**Experience**

* 10+ years in a single or multi-family office, private banking service and operations, Big Four compliance or tax, or a similar multi-entity financial operations role.
* Familiarity with property documentation and mutation processes, and with company secretarial records. This is an additional requirement not mandatory.

**Core Attributes**

**Ownership**
: Takes responsibility from initiation through completion.

**Organisation:**
A high standard of personal organisation, and comfort bringing structure to complex, multi- party processes.

**Judgement:**
A clear sense of which decisions sit with the role, which belong to the family, and which require a professional's sign-off.

**Attention to detail:**
Comfortable working with financial records, regulatory filings, entity structures and historical transaction data where accuracy is critical.

**Composure**
: Steadiness under a calendar of statutory deadlines that do not move.

**Communication:**
Able to communicate comfortably with family members, senior advisors, bankers, lawyers, accountants and investment professionals.

**Discretion:**
Absolute confidentiality is non-negotiable. The role involves access to highly sensitive family, financial, investment and personal information.

title: Consultant - Business Consulting Risk - Compliance and Technology Transformation - PAN INDIA
description:

**Consultant - Business Consulting Risk - Compliance and Technology Transformation - PAN INDIA**
**FS :**
Finance fuels our lives. Banking, Insurance and Wealth management, create the foundations for growth, prosperity and peace of mind. No other Industry touches so many people or shapes so many lives.
  
  
Amid sweeping regulatory change, today’s financial services institutions are focusing on digital transformation, convergence and disruption from an array of nontraditional competitors — all while meeting greater demands for trust and transparency.
  
  
To address this delicate balance of issues, our competent team of business strategists, technologists and industry leaders bring fresh thinking and sector knowledge across banking and capital markets, insurance, and wealth and asset management. The results are seamless collaboration, innovative problem solving, breakthrough performance gains and sustainable value creation.
  
  
We recruit, train and nurture a diverse set of people who dedicate their minds to building the future of financial services. Together, we explore new perspectives with innovative and entrepreneurial thinking to deliver exceptional client service and ensure that what we do today, counts for tomorrow.
  
  
**CNS - Risk - Process & Controls :**
EY Consulting is building a better working world by transforming businesses through the power of people, technology and innovation. Our client-centric approach focuses on driving long-term value for our clients by solving their most strategic problems. EY Consulting is made up of three sub-service lines: Business Consulting (including Performance Improvement and Risk Consulting), Technology Consulting and People Advisory Services.
  
  
We help our clients in identifying and managing the interplay between upside and downside risk in order to make the long-term decisions to prevent risk and impact on their organization's ability to meet its future business strategy and objectives. The 3 key fields of play are :
  
  
Financial Services Risk - helps clients in the financial sector to identify, manage and monitor the risks in their business. It is done through a transformative and agile approach including process and procedures, risk, data modeling and analytics, reporting to stakeholders and third parties, business requirements (for software selection and IT implementation), analysis of assets and liabilities, and capital and liquidity management.
  
  
**Your Key Responsibilities**
**Technical Excellence**

* Risk & Compliance Transformation

+ Support the assessment, design, and implementation of risk, compliance, and governance frameworks.
+ Work with clients to improve monitoring, controls, reporting, and regulatory compliance processes.
+ Assist in identifying opportunities for process optimization, automation, and control enhancement.
+ Support transformation initiatives related to risk management, compliance monitoring, operational risk, governance, and internal controls.

**Business Analysis & Solution Delivery**




+ Gather business requirements through workshops, interviews, and stakeholder discussions.
+ Develop business requirement documents, functional specifications, user stories, and process maps.
+ Perform current-state and target-state assessments and identify transformation opportunities.
+ Support end-to-end project delivery including requirements management, testing, deployment, and change management.

**Technology & Digital Transformation**




+ Collaborate with technology teams to implement workflow, governance, compliance, and risk management solutions.
+ Evaluate and recommend technology-enabled solutions to address business and regulatory challenges.
+ Support implementation of GRC, risk management, compliance monitoring, workflow, and reporting platforms.
+ Leverage data analytics and dashboarding to improve decision-making and governance reporting.

**AI & Emerging Technology**




+ Help clients identify and prioritize AI, GenAI, and intelligent automation use cases across risk and compliance functions.
+ Support development of AI-enabled solutions for regulatory intelligence, policy management, document review, reporting, and knowledge management.
+ Assist in defining business requirements, governance considerations, and adoption strategies for AI-driven initiatives.
+ Evaluate opportunities to enhance risk and compliance processes through automation, predictive insights, and advanced analytics.

**Stakeholder & Project Management**




+ Work closely with client stakeholders across Risk, Compliance, Technology, Operations, and Business functions.
+ Support project governance, status reporting, issue tracking, and executive presentations.
+ Coordinate with cross-functional teams to ensure timely delivery of project milestones.

**Skills And Attributes**
**To qualify for the role you must have**
**Qualification**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Technology, Business, Finance, or a related discipline.
* 4-6 years of experience in Risk Consulting, Compliance, Business Analysis, Technology Transformation, Banking, Financial Services, or related domains.
* Experience in regulatory, compliance, governance, risk, or transformation initiatives.
* Strong analytical and stakeholder management skills.

**What We Look For**
People with the ability to work in a collaborative manner to provide services across multiple client departments while following the commercial and legal requirements. You will need a practical approach to solving issues and complex problems with the ability to deliver insightful and practical solutions. We look for people who are agile, curious, mindful, and able to sustain positive energy, while being adaptable and creative in their approach.
  
  
**What We Offer**
Fuelled by the brilliance of our people, EY has emerged as the strongest brand and the most attractive employer in our field, with market-leading growth over competitors. Our people work side-by-side with market-leading entrepreneurs, game-changers, disruptors, and visionaries. As an organization, we are investing more time, technology, and money than ever before in skills and learning for our people. At EY, you will have a personalized Career Journey and also the chance to tap into the resources of our career frameworks to better know about your roles, skills, and opportunities.
  
  
EY is equally committed to being an inclusive employer, and we strive to achieve the right balance for our people—enabling us to deliver excellent client service while allowing our people to build their careers as well as focus on their wellbeing.
  
  
If you can confidently demonstrate that you meet the criteria above, please contact us as soon as possible.
  
  
Join us in shaping the future with confidence. Apply Now

The
**Compliance Manager**
, based at our Head Office in Gurugram, India, will support the implementation of the Group Compliance Programme and promote a strong culture of ethics, integrity and compliance across the business.
  
  
The role will focus on compliance risk management, ethics and compliance processes, investigations, third-party due diligence, monitoring and stakeholder engagement.

title: Lead Network Policy
description:
**The Role**
This role will be responsible for shaping and supporting policy and regulatory frameworks impacting digital commerce in India, while driving ONDC’s engagement with government and regulatory stakeholders.
  
  
The individual will work closely with ministries, regulators, and public institutions to enable policy alignment, support regulatory development, and strengthen ONDC’s positioning within the evolving digital commerce ecosystem.
  
  
Additionally, the role will contribute to the techno-legal framework for network governance, including the design of systems and mechanisms to monitor and ensure policy compliance across the network.
  
  
This position sits at the intersection of public policy, regulatory affairs, and government engagement, requiring both strategic thinking and execution capability.
  
  
**What You'll Own**

* Government & Policy Engagement: engage with government entities and regulatory bodies on matters related to digital commerce and network-based platforms.
* Build and manage relationships with key policymakers, ministries, and regulatory stakeholders; represent ONDC in policy forums, consultations, working groups, and government discussions.
* Policy & Regulatory Development: track and interpret developments across e-commerce policy, digital trade, competition, and data governance frameworks — including the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and related rules.
* Contribute to policy notes, consultation responses, discussion papers, and regulatory submissions; support the development of policy recommendations relevant to ONDC.
* Work on key themes such as platform neutrality, interoperability, digital inclusion, and network governance.
* Research & Policy Analysis: conduct in-depth policy research, regulatory analysis, and impact assessments; develop briefing notes, policy papers, and executive presentations for leadership and external stakeholders.
* Prepare management reports and information packs — in particular for regulator meetings, internal reviews, and committee presentations — ensuring timely and accurate reporting.
* Stakeholder & Ecosystem Management: engage with industry bodies, think tanks, research institutions, and ecosystem participants; collaborate closely with legal, operations, technology, and leadership.
* Capability Building: deliver training sessions and regulatory updates to product teams and the wider business, and build scalable processes, templates, and documentation for the team as it grows.

**What Success Looks Like**
You become ONDC’s trusted voice on policy — tracking regulatory change before it lands, translating it into practical guidance for the business, and representing ONDC credibly with ministries, regulators, and institutions.
  
  
**What We're Looking For**

* 8+ years in public policy, regulatory affairs, or government engagement — preferably in digital, technology, or e-commerce sectors.
* Strong understanding of India’s regulatory landscape, policy-making processes, and frameworks including the DPDP Act.
* Excellent research, writing, stakeholder management, and communication skills, with the ability to translate policy into actionable frameworks.
* Comfortable working in a cross-functional, high-impact environment, with strong interpersonal skills for internal and external stakeholder collaboration.

We’re proud to have been helping our clients build better financial futures for over 50 years. How have we achieved this? By working together - and supporting each other - all over the world. So, join our General Counsel Shared Services Team and feel like you’re part of something bigger.
  
  
**General Counsel Shared Services**
General Counsel (GC) is a trusted advisor to all parts of Fidelity International Limited (“FIL”), providing high-value independent advisory and assurance expertise through our specialist teams. GC comprises Legal, Risk, Compliance, Tax, and Public Policy & Strategic Relationship Management. The GC Shared Services function is a global centre of expertise currently located in Dalian and India, providing operational support and services to the General Counsel function.
  
  
**Global Investment Compliance:**
The Global Investment Compliance (GIC) function provides advice, support, oversight and challenge to teams across Fidelity’s Asset Management Platforms. Stakeholders include portfolio managers, research analysts, trading desks, corporate finance, institutional teams and their respective support groups.
  
  
**Investment Compliance Monitoring:**
The Investment Compliance Monitoring team forms a crucial component of the Global Investment Compliance department, with teams located in Japan, Hong Kong, London, and Gurgaon. The team supports the implementation and continuous execution of trading, communication, and other regulatory surveillance processes. This involves examining alerts, identifying potential market abuse or misconduct, escalating issues, supporting investigations, and strengthening surveillance controls. The team works closely with global stakeholders, supports system testing and optimisation, and plays a key role in enhancing processes and maintaining thorough documentation.
  
  
**About Your Role**
The role supports monitoring trading activity in stocks listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and other relevant market conduct surveillance activities. You will be responsible for monitoring trading in accordance with market regulations and guidelines to detect suspicious transactions that might constitute market abuse. In addition, there will be opportunities to perform other activities undertaken by the firm’s Investment Compliance function.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Using proprietary and market-leading tools to perform recurring exception monitoring of FIL’s trading and other investment activities and investigates exceptions and incidents which include, but not limited to, best execution, fair allocation, market conduct, and conflicts of interest;
* Respond to requests and inquiries from regulators, exchanges and industry bodies, including the SESC, KLFB, JSDA, JPX, and IMAJ..
* Assisting with thematic reviews, desktop reviews and projects;
* Coordinate and collaborate with internal teams in relation to periodic regulatory supervisory inspections.
* Supporting the monitoring and analysis of regulatory trends and changes to the various rules and regulations impacting FIL’s investment functions and working closely with and advising internal stakeholders on the impact of such trends and changes.
* Supporting the development, review and implementation of changes to policies and procedures related to FIL’s investment functions.
* Develop effective working relationships with other functional areas to support the timely receipt of information required to complete monitoring and review activities.
* Provide a high-quality and timely service to internal stakeholders.

**Experience And Qualifications Required**

* Strong analytical capabilities and excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Native Japanese speaker or highly fluent in Japanese, demonstrated by successful completion of JLPT N1. Fluency in English is also required.
* 7+ years of experience in the financial services industry in an oversight, compliance monitoring, surveillance, or securities operations capacity, with a firm understanding of concepts and practices relating to equities trading.
* Good understanding of Japanese regulations and market practices, including but not limited to the Financial Instruments Exchange Law, JSDA Rules and Guidelines, and the Tokyo Stock Exchange Regulations.
* Experience responding to regulator or exchange enquiries, supporting regulatory inspections, or assisting with investigations would be advantageous.
* Strong ability to analyse trading activity, identify unusual patterns, document investigation outcomes and escalate issues appropriately.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills in Japanese and English.
* Practical knowledge and skilled in using MS Office applications, especially PowerPoint, Excel and Word.
* Professional certification such as JSDA Internal Control Supervisor (Naibu Kanri Sekininsha) qualification or CAMS, CISI, CFA, FRM, or CPA is desirable but not essential.
* A global perspective and cultural awareness, with the ability to work effectively across regions and time zones.
* Strong attention to detail, accuracy, and investigative discipline, with professional scepticism and sound judgement.
* High degree of integrity, discretion, and ability to handle confidential or sensitive matters.
* Ability to collaborate effectively with stakeholders, clearly articulate issues to senior management, and challenge constructively where required.
* Strong self-motivation, organisation, prioritisation, and time management skills. Positive team player with the ability to work independently and take initiative.

**Feel rewarded**
For starters, we’ll offer you a comprehensive benefits package. We’ll value your wellbeing and support your development. And we’ll be as flexible as we can about where and when you work – finding a balance that works for all of us. It’s all part of our commitment to making you feel motivated by the work you do and happy to be part of our team. For more about our work, our approach to dynamic working and how you could build your future here, visit careers.fidelityinternational.com.

title: Manager, Resposible AI, GESS - Global Capability Center
description:
**Description**
**About Alvarez & Marsal**
Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with entrepreneurial, action and results-oriented professionals. We take a hands-on approach to solving our clients' problems and assisting them in reaching their potential. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact our clients and shape our industry. The collaborative environment and engaging work - guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity - are why our people love working at A&M.
  
  
**The Team**
You will be joining a newly formed Global AI & Knowledge Organization (GAIKO) led by a Chief AI & Knowledge Officer who is moving fast. The team is global, still being staffed, and operating with urgency. The broader team includes a product & tech pillar, change management, KM services, operations and value & governance.
  
  
**How You Will Contribute**

* AI Governance & Policy
* Working in partnership with the GAIKO + IT+ Risk + InfoSec and with support of the AI Operating Committee (AIOC), help design and operationalize the firm's global Responsible AI framework, including policies, standards, intake processes, use case approvals, and risk escalation procedures.
* Define the firm’s end-to-end pathway for creating and deploying AI — who may build, in which environments (including sandbox standards for prototyping and experimentation), what data controls apply at each stage, and the gates, criteria, and approval forums required to move work from internal experimentation to client-facing deployment — integrating with, rather than duplicating, existing technology risk review forums.[C1.1]
* Provide RAI assessments of proposed AI tools and partnerships, evaluating data residency, confidentiality, bias, and compliance risk. This includes independently supporting the evaluation of vendors’ technical architecture and data-handling claims, in partnership with Information Security.
* Co-own and maintain, with GSO and other designated stakeholders, [JB2.1][C2.2]the firm's AI Responsible Use guidelines, updating them as the regulatory landscape evolves across key jurisdictions (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, GDPR, India DPDP Act, and others).
* Define the RAI function's charter, roadmap, and KPIs in collaboration with the other relevant stakeholders; build the operating model for how RAI integrates with risk, delivery, legal, compliance, and IT security teams globally.
* Serve as a firm-wide subject matter expert on AI governance, policy, and responsible use strategy.
* Ethics & Bias Review
* Design and lead a repeatable pre-deployment ethics review process for AI models and tools, including fairness audits, bias testing, impact assessments, documentation standards, escalation paths, and sign-off criteria.
* Build and strengthen client AI case review processes ensuring that AI used in client engagements meets appropriate standards for transparency, bias, accuracy, and data handling before delivery.
* Build playbooks and toolkits that embed responsible AI principles into project delivery lifecycles across all practice areas and geographies.
* Partner closely with the Change Management function to weave RAI messaging into the firm's broader AI adoption and culture change agenda, making responsible use a visible, positive part of the firm's AI transformation, not a compliance afterthought.
* AI Risk & Audit
* Define and manage a global AI risk taxonomy and register; assess risk across the full AI lifecycle (data sourcing, model development, deployment, monitoring, and decommissioning).
* Establish audit and monitoring mechanisms for production AI systems, including tracking for model drift, performance degradation, data handling violations, and regulatory compliance gaps.
* Collaborate with Legal, Compliance, and IT Security to ensure all AI deployments meet applicable data privacy, security, and regulatory requirements across jurisdictions.
* Serve as the RAI technical counterpart to Information Security across all AI work including vendor tools, internally built solutions, agentic workflows, and engagement-team prototypes, and jointly evaluating data handling, controls, security architecture, and residency.
* Prepare and deliver executive-level risk reporting on the firm's AI risk posture for the AIOC and, where required, for escalation to the AI Board or client audiences.

**Qualifications**

* 8–12 years of total experience, with at least 2 years focused on AI governance, responsible AI, technology risk, or a closely related discipline.
* Demonstrated experience building a governance framework, risk program, or compliance function. Prior experience standing up a new function or practice is strongly preferred.
* Hands-on technical experience assessing AI/ML systems: data flows and pipelines, model development lifecycles, API and integration architecture (including agentic patterns and MCP-style integrations), cloud data residency and security controls, and common bias and fairness methodologies.
* Ability to independently evaluate a vendor’s technical and data-handling claims and partner credibly with information security teams on assessments — challenging technical evidence, not only summarizing it.
* Career background in ML engineering, data engineering, security/GRC engineering, or technology risk with demonstrable technical depth. Candidates whose experience is exclusively policy or legal are unlikely to meet the technical bar for this role.
* Solid command of key regulatory and standards frameworks relevant to a global consulting firm: EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, GDPR, and India's DPDP Act.
* Ability to operate effectively across geographies and time zones; comfortable collaborating with a primarily USbased leadership team from an India-based position.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to translate complex risk and governance concepts for both technical practitioners and C-suite audiences.
* Proven ability to influence without authority in a matrixed, fast-paced professional services environment.

**Your journey at A&M**
We recognize that our people are the driving force behind our success, which is why we prioritize an employee experience that fosters each person’s unique professional and personal development. Our robust performance development process promotes continuous learning, rewards your contributions, and fosters a culture of meritocracy. With top-notch training and on-the-job learning opportunities, you can acquire new skills and advance your career. We prioritize your well-being, providing benefits and resources to support you on your personal journey. Our people consistently highlight the growth opportunities, our unique, entrepreneurial culture, and the fun we have together as their favorite aspects of working at A&M. The possibilities are endless for high-performing and passionate professionals.

•  Learning and growth in a dynamic environment

title: Compliance Analyst, Expert Network
description:
**About AlphaSense**
The world’s most sophisticated companies rely on AlphaSense to remove uncertainty from decision-making. With market intelligence and search built on proven AI, AlphaSense delivers insights that matter from content you can trust. Our universe of public and private content includes equity research, company filings, event transcripts, expert calls, news, trade journals, and clients’ own research content.
  
  
The acquisition of Tegus by AlphaSense in 2024 advances our shared mission to empower professionals to make smarter decisions through AI-driven market intelligence. Together, AlphaSense and Tegus will accelerate growth, innovation, and content expansion, with complementary product and content capabilities that enable users to unearth even more comprehensive insights from thousands of content sets. Our platform is trusted by over 6,000 enterprise customers, including a majority of the S&P 500. Founded in 2011, AlphaSense is headquartered in New York City with more than 2,000 employees across the globe and offices in the U.S., U.K., Finland, India, Singapore, Canada, and Ireland. Come join us!
  
  
**About The Role**
The Compliance Analyst, Expert Network plays an important role in supporting the day-to-day compliance needs of AlphaSense's Expert Network business. Reporting to the Head of Expert Network, this role supports expert sourcing and onboarding, client compliance onboarding and inquiries, and other compliance questions that arise across the Expert Network business.
  
  
As part of the Compliance team, the Compliance Analyst will help review experts being considered for client projects, apply AlphaSense's sourcing and compliance policies, and provide guidance to the teams responsible for sourcing experts. The role will also support client-specific compliance requirements and help respond to questions and concerns from clients about AlphaSense's Expert Network compliance practices.
  
  
This role is well suited for someone who is interested in developing experience in compliance within a fast-paced technology company. The analyst will receive training on AlphaSense's Expert Network business, compliance policies, and sourcing requirements and will learn how to apply that guidance to different situations and when to escalate questions for additional review.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Review prospective experts for client projects to identify potential compliance considerations and determine whether they can be sourced in accordance with AlphaSense's policies and client-specific requirements.
* Conduct expert onboarding and compliance reviews, including assessing current and prior employment, the companies and topics experts may be asked to discuss, confidentiality obligations, and potential material non-public information (MNPI) concerns.
* Serve as a day-to-day compliance resource for teams sourcing experts, providing guidance on sourcing requirements, reviewing questions that arise throughout the sourcing process, and escalating complex or higher-risk matters as appropriate.
* Support the compliance aspects of client onboarding by reviewing client-specific requirements and restrictions, establishing appropriate sourcing protocols, and ensuring requirements are accurately communicated and implemented.
* Support ongoing client compliance needs by responding to questions and concerns, assisting with due diligence requests and compliance questionnaires, and providing information regarding AlphaSense's Expert Network compliance policies and processes.
* Address compliance matters that arise in the day-to-day operation of the Expert Network business, applying established policies and procedures and coordinating with Legal and other internal stakeholders when additional review is required.
* Maintain accurate records of compliance reviews, decisions, and client requirements, and contribute to the development and maintenance of compliance policies, procedures, internal guidance, and training materials.

**Who You Are**

* 2-4 years of experience in compliance, legal, operations, customer support, financial services, or another role involving research, analysis, or process-based work is helpful. Recent graduates are encouraged to apply.
* Interested in developing knowledge of compliance concepts relevant to expert networks, including confidentiality, material non-public information (MNPI), and insider trading considerations. Prior experience with these topics is helpful but not required; role-specific training will be provided.
* Highly detail-oriented, with the ability to review information carefully, identify relevant details, and consistently apply established policies and procedures.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an interest in working through different scenarios and using established guidance to determine the appropriate next steps.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to communicate clearly and professionally with both internal teams and clients.
* Organized and reliable, with the ability to manage multiple requests, prioritize work, and maintain accuracy in a fast-paced environment.
* Sound judgment, including knowing when a question can be addressed using established guidance and when it should be escalated for additional review.
* Comfortable learning and working with new systems, tools, and technology used to support compliance processes.

AlphaSense is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals. All employees share in the responsibility for fulfilling AlphaSense’s commitment to equal employment opportunity. AlphaSense does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of race, color, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, religion, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, military or veteran status, disability, or any other non-merit factor. This policy applies to every aspect of employment at AlphaSense, including recruitment, hiring, training, advancement, and termination.
  
  
In addition, it is the policy of AlphaSense to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where a particular employee works.
  
  
Recruiting Scams and Fraud
  
  
We At AlphaSense Have Been Made Aware Of Fraudulent Job Postings And Individuals Impersonating AlphaSense Recruiters. These Scams May Involve Fake Job Offers, Requests For Sensitive Personal Information, Or Demands For Payment. Please Note
  
  

* AlphaSense never asks candidates to pay for job applications, equipment, or training.
* All official communications will come from an @alpha-sense.com email address.
* If you’re unsure about a job posting or recruiter, verify it on our Careers page.

If you believe you’ve been targeted by a scam or have any doubts regarding the authenticity of any job listing purportedly from or on behalf of AlphaSense please contact us. Your security and trust matter to us.

title: VP - Public Policy & Government Affairs
description:
**Vice President - Public Policy & Government Affairs**
**Company**
: CoinDCX
  
  
**Location**
: Delhi, India
  
  
**About CoinDCX:**
Established in 2018, CoinDCX is India’s largest Virtual Digital Asset (VDA) exchange platform and a foundational force in the global Web3 ecosystem. Trusted by over 2 crore registered users, we have invested in 15+ Web3 projects and startups globally.
  
  
As a compliance-first organization, CoinDCX was the first Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP) to register with the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) in India. With licensed operations spanning the UAE and Bahrain, our mission is to democratize investment in VDAs, provide seamless access to Web3 experiences, and relentlessly protect user interests.
  
  
**About The Role**
We are seeking an exceptionally credentialed Vice President - Public Policy & Government Affairs to spearhead our strategic advocacy efforts, shaping forward-looking regulatory frameworks for the Web3 and crypto industry across India and global markets.
  
  
Reporting directly to the Chief Public Policy Officer, you will lead a dedicated team of policy professionals and work closely with the executive management team. You will design and execute 360-degree policy strategies, drive public-facing advocacy, build strategic alliances, and serve as a crucial liaison between CoinDCX and regulatory bodies, government entities, and industry associations.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Strategic Advocacy & Public Policy:
* Policy Strategy Formulation: Develop and execute proactive, high-impact policy advocacy strategies to support the sustainable growth of the Web3 and digital asset ecosystem in India and internationally.
* 360-Degree Advocacy Plans: Collaborate with the Chief Public Policy Officer and executive leadership to align policy research, external representations, and internal business objectives.
* Public Policy Communications: Lead the strategy for public-facing policy artifacts—including white papers, official representations, research reports, and opinion pieces—working alongside Legal, Compliance, PR, Marketing, and external vendors.
* Policy Intelligence: Continuously monitor, analyze, and forecast regulatory trends and policy developments, delivering actionable guidance on potential risks and proactive engagement opportunities.
* Stakeholder Engagement & Ecosystem Alliances:
* Government & Regulatory Relations: Cultivate and sustain deep, trusted relationships with key government officials, financial regulators, law enforcement agencies, academia, and civil society.
* Industry Leadership: Represent CoinDCX in global and regional Web3, fintech, and trade associations to drive collaborative industry alignment and self-regulatory initiatives.
* Thought Leadership: Serve as a primary spokesperson for the company at high-level industry forums, roundtables, and policy summits.
* Cross-Functional Advisory & Team Leadership:
* Internal Strategic Counsel: Provide clear, business-enabling regulatory guidance to cross-functional teams—including Legal, Compliance, Product, and Engineering—on emerging legislative requirements.
* Team Development: Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team of government affairs and policy professionals, fostering a culture of excellence and accountability.

**Key Requirements:**

* Experience: 12+ years of progressive leadership in public policy, government affairs, or regulatory strategy, ideally within the technology, fintech, or digital asset sectors.
* Regulatory Expertise: Deep understanding of the Indian regulatory ecosystem, parliamentary processes, financial regulatory bodies, and law enforcement frameworks, combined with global regulatory exposure (e.g., UAE, Bahrain, international markets).
* Track Record: Demonstrated success in conceptualizing and delivering impactful policy advocacy campaigns that yielded tangible regulatory or industry outcomes.
* Stakeholder Network: Proven experience building high-trust relationships across government entities, regulatory authorities, trade bodies, and policy think tanks.
* Leadership Skills: Proven capacity to manage, mentor, and scale team members while coordinating effectively across internal business units.
* Communication: Outstanding oral, written, and narrative-building skills, with the ability to translate complex technical/financial Web3 concepts into compelling policy positions.
* Education: Advanced degree (Master’s or equivalent) in Public Policy, Law, Economics, International Relations, or a related field preferred.

**Core Skills**

* Government engagement and stakeholder management.
* Policy analysis, advocacy, and drafting.
* Strategic communications and executive advisory.
* Regulatory risk assessment and issue anticipation.
* Cross-functional leadership and alignment.
* High-quality writing, structured thinking, and attention to detail.
* Strong credibility, discretion, and judgment under pressure.

**What Success Looks Like**

* The company is consistently represented as a credible, constructive, and informed voice in policy discussions relevant to Crypto and Web3 in India.
* The leadership team receive timely, high-quality advice on policy developments, stakeholder engagement, and reputational risks.
* The company’s policy priorities are clearly articulated in external forums and reflected in stronger stakeholder relationships and better-informed regulatory dialogue.
* Internal teams are equipped with actionable policy intelligence that supports business continuity, compliance readiness, and strategic decision-making.

**Why This Role Matters & What’s In It For You**
At CoinDCX, this role is central to shaping how India’s crypto and Web3 ecosystem evolves. You will work closely with leadership, regulators, and policymakers to help drive constructive regulation, industry credibility, and long-term growth for the sector.
  
  

* Opportunity to influence one of India’s most dynamic and high-impact sectors.
* Direct exposure to the CEO and strategic decision-making.
* Lead policy conversations with top government and regulatory stakeholders.
* Build institutional influence in a fast-evolving industry at national scale.

**Hiring Process**
Here’s what your journey with us looks like:
  
  

* Application Review – We assess for skills, alignment, and intent
* Recruiter Connect – A short conversation to understand you better
* Functional Round(s) – Deep dive into your approach, craft, and problem-solving
* Assignment / Simulation Round (if required) – A take-home task or live problem-solving exercise to understand how you think and execute in real scenarios
* Culture & Values Discussion – A conversation to understand our ways of working and how you thrive best
* Founder Conversation – For certain roles and senior levels, you may meet our founders to explore strategic alignment and long-term fit

**Where We Work**
We believe the best ideas emerge when people build together. Collaboration, speed and trust come alive when teams share the same space.
  
  
With this belief, we operate as a work-from-office organisation. This role is based out of our
**Delhi Office**
, where energy, alignment and innovation move in real time.
  
  
**Perks That Empower You**
We believe great people deserve great experiences.
  
  

* Design Your Own Benefits: Flexible perks to match your lifestyle
* Unlimited Wellness Leaves: Rest and recharge as you need
* Mental Wellness Support: Access to therapy and wellness resources
* Learning Sessions: Bi-weekly learning and growth opportunities

**Ready to Build What’s Next?**
If you’re looking for a role that gives you direct access to high-stakes decisions, deep impact and a chance to build the future of finance, this is it.
  
  
Join CoinDCX and help us make crypto accessible to every Indian, together.

**4. Intellectual Property & Brand Protection**

* Manage trademark, design and copyright filings, renewals, oppositions and licence recordals, in coordination with licensors and IP counsel.
* Support licensors and IP counsel in taking action against counterfeit and grey-market goods, including marketplace takedowns, customs recordal and enforcement notices.

**5. Regulatory & Statutory Compliance**

* Ensure compliance with applicable corporate, labour, shops and establishment, contract labour, POSH, consumer protection, e-commerce, Legal Metrology, customs, FEMA and MSME laws and regulations.
* Maintain the compliance calendar and legal records, liaise with regulators, and track regulatory changes and their business impact.

**6. Data Protection & Technology**

* Ensure compliance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, including privacy policies, consent, data-processing terms and data breach response.
* Review technology, platform, payment gateway and marketplace agreements, as well as advertising, influencer and collaboration agreements.

**7. Disputes & Litigation**

* Draft legal notices and replies; appoint and manage external counsel; track matters across landlord, vendor, consumer, IP, customs and tax disputes.
* Maintain the litigation register, report case status to management, and provide litigation and contingent-liability information to Finance and auditors.

**8. Corporate, Banking & Transactions**

* Coordinate with the Company Secretary on ROC filings, board and shareholder matters, and inter-company and related-party agreements.
* Review bank facility documents, letters of credit and guarantees, and support security creation and charge filings.
* Support due diligence, fundraising, joint ventures, business transfers and M&A, as required.

**9. Business Partnering & Governance**

* Advise Finance, HR, Sales, Marketing, Supply Chain and Operations on legal risk; support HR with employment documentation, policies and employee-related legal matters.
* Strengthen legal processes and policies, conduct training on contract and compliance fundamentals, and report on legal matters to management.

**Job Requirements:**

* **Qualification:**
  LL.B. / BA LL.B. from a recognised institution (mandatory)
* **Experience:**
  5–8 years post-qualification in corporate legal, commercial contracts or an in-house legal role, preferably in fashion, apparel, lifestyle or consumer retail with import exposure
* **Contract Drafting & Negotiation:**
  Demonstrated expertise in independently drafting and negotiating licence, distribution, lease, consignment and job-work agreements, with the ability to negotiate key commercial and risk terms (liability, indemnity, exclusivity, royalty and minimum commitments) with international licensors, landlords and other institutional counterparties.
* **Property & Stamp Law:**
  Sound understanding of the Transfer of Property Act, the Registration Act, state stamp duty regulations and title due diligence, with a track record of executing leases across multiple states.
* **IP & Regulatory Knowledge:**
  Working knowledge of the Trade Marks, Designs and Copyright Acts; the Companies Act; FEMA; customs; labour and shops and establishment laws; Legal Metrology; consumer protection and e-commerce regulations; and the DPDP Act, with sound judgement on when to engage specialist counsel.
* **Dispute & Counsel Management:**
  Familiarity with civil procedure, limitation, arbitration and recovery mechanisms, and the ability to instruct external counsel, manage cost and scope, and give management a clear assessment of legal exposure.
* **Financial Acumen:**
  Ability to interpret royalty, minimum guarantee, landed-cost, working-capital, letter of credit and bank guarantee terms, ensuring that contracts align with the company's accounting and funding requirements.
* **Commercial Judgement:**
  A pragmatic, business-minded approach to legal risk: prioritising issues by business impact, recommending workable solutions and delivering advice within business timelines.
* **Communication & Stakeholder Management:**
  Strong ability to communicate legal risk clearly to business teams and senior management, and to engage credibly with licensors, landlords, bankers, auditors, regulators and external counsel.
* **Ownership & Organisation:**
  Self-motivated and deadline-driven, with strong documentation discipline; able to maintain a contract tracker and compliance calendar, exercise discretion with confidential information, and build legal processes and, over time, a small team.

title: Head – Compliance

● Manage regulatory matters involving customer complaints, escalations and sensitive compliance issues, ensuring appropriate resolution and reporting.

● Build a strong compliance culture across the organisation through training, awareness and ongoing monitoring.

● Strong understanding of the RBI regulatory framework applicable to NBFCs.

● Experience in NBFC compliance, regulatory reporting, KYC/AML, digital lending and customer protection regulations.

● Ability to independently interpret regulations and translate them into actionable business requirements.

● Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, particularly with senior management, Board members and regulators.

● Strong judgement, ownership and ability to manage high-pressure and sensitive regulatory situations.

● Experience managing and developing a compliance team.

Preferred Profile

● Candidate currently or recently working as Head/VP/AVP – Compliance, Chief Compliance Officer, or senior regulatory/compliance leader in an NBFC.

● Experience with RBI-regulated lending / digital lending businesses will be highly preferred.

● Prior experience of directly managing RBI inspections and regulatory correspondence/escalations is essential.

● Exposure to Board-level compliance reporting and Audit/Risk Committee interactions is preferred.

* Support contract compliance, pricing reviews, renewal strategy, commercial governance, cost optimization, and vendor consolidation initiatives.

* Enable AI-led workflow automation, GenAI-assisted reporting, predictive analytics, anomaly detection, exception management, decision intelligence, and intelligent governance dashboards.

40

title: Manager – Travel, T&E Compliance, Audit & Reporting
description:
**Job Description**
Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc., (ACT) is a global Fortune 200 company (https://corpo.couche-tard.com/en/). A leader in convenience store and fuel space, it has a footprint across 31 countries and territories. ACT's India entity i.e. Circle K Business Centre India (CKBCI) is a wholly owned subsidiary and an integrated center, collaborating with our international teams supporting the delivery of ACT's global business operations.
  
  
**About The Role**
This role will be based in Cyber Hub Gurugram. Manager – Travel, T&E Compliance, Audit & Reporting will be responsible for the day-to-day governance, compliance, controls, reporting and continuous improvement of Circle K's Travel & Expense (T&E) programme and day to day governance of Travel Management Company (TMC).
  
  
The role will act as a central point of expertise for travel operations, TMC governance, T&E policy compliance, audit and controls, travel policy standardization, management reporting, training and process automation. The position will work closely with Finance, Procurement, Internal Audit, HR, Technology, business stakeholders, Navan/ Travel Management Company (TMC) to ensure that T&E processes are controlled, efficient, data-led and aligned with Circle K policies and internal-control and audit requirements.
  
  
The role will also lead opportunities to leverage automation and analytics to strengthen preventive controls, reduce manual effort, improve compliance and identify savings and leakage across the T&E ecosystem.
  
  
***Roles & Responsibilities
  
  
Travel & T&E Operations***

* Manage and oversee the day-to-day execution of the global T&E operating processes, with particular focus on travel booked through Navan and related travel expenses.
* Work closely with Director CKBCI to be the operational subject-matter expert for Navan, including policy configuration, traveller profiles, approval workflows, reporting, exceptions, and issue resolution.
* Monitor the end-to-end travel process from travel request and approval through booking, travel, expense submission, reimbursement and reconciliation.
* Establish and maintain clear procedures for handling travel and T&E exceptions, escalations, cancellations, refunds, and credits.
* Partner with the TMC, and other suppliers to monitor service levels and resolve recurring operational issues.

***T&E Compliance & Policy Governance***

* Monitor compliance with the Global T&E Policies and identify areas of non-compliance, control gaps and emerging risks.
* Develop and maintain a structured T&E compliance framework, including preventive and corrective controls.
* Monitor advance-booking compliance, pre-trip approval, preferred supplier usage, policy exceptions, out-of-channel bookings and other defined policy requirements.
* Ensure policies and policy changes are accurately translated into system rules, workflows and automated controls.
* Establish appropriate compliance mechanisms for different traveller groups, including executives, while maintaining appropriate visibility and governance.
* Coordinate policy communication, training and periodic awareness initiatives with HR and business stakeholders

**Audit, Controls & Risk Management**

* Own the operational response to T&E audit requirements and support Internal Audit, Finance and other control functions with evidence and analysis.
* Ensure T&E processes and automated reviews comply with internal policies, regulatory requirements, fraud-prevention controls and SOX/internal-control expectations, where applicable.
* Validate the effectiveness and accuracy of automated and AI-enabled T&E controls before and after implementation.
* Maintain audit trails, control documentation, standard operating procedures and evidence of exception resolution.
* Identify control weaknesses and recommend remediation actions with clear owners and timelines.
* Monitor recurring exceptions and investigate potential misuse, fraud, duplicate transactions or unusual spending patterns.

***Reporting, Analytics & Insights***

* Develop and maintain a T&E management reporting and dashboard framework covering spend, compliance, adoption, leakage, suppliers, exceptions and savings.
* Provide regular reporting to Finance, Procurement, leadership and other relevant stakeholders.
* Analyse travel spend across business units, traveller groups, suppliers, routes, categories and booking channels to identify trends and opportunities.
* Establish meaningful KPIs and dashboards to measure the effectiveness of the T&E programme.
* Develop reporting that provides visibility of Navan adoption versus off-platform spend, including root-cause analysis of leakage.
* Translate T&E data into actionable recommendations for policy, sourcing, supplier management and process improvement.

***Process Improvement, Standardization & Automation***

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives across the T&E process, with a focus on reducing manual intervention and strengthening controls.
* Identify opportunities to use RPA, workflow automation and analytics to improve T&E compliance and operational efficiency.
* Develop automated controls for areas such as:
* advance-booking compliance.
* pre-trip approval.
* policy exception monitoring.
* duplicate and high-risk expense detection.
* unused travel credit tracking.
* refund monitoring.
* off-platform booking/leakage detection; and
* automated compliance reporting.
* Work with Technology and business teams to define requirements, test solutions, validate outputs and transition automation into business-as-usual operations.
* Continuously assess whether existing controls can be simplified, automated or moved from detective to preventive controls.

***Travel Spend & Supplier Governance***

* Partner with Procurement to identify travel savings and supplier optimisation opportunities.
* Monitor utilisation of negotiated airline, hotel, car rental and other travel rates.
* Analyse supplier and channel performance and identify opportunities for consolidation or improved commercial terms.
* Support supplier reviews, RFPs and contract renewals with data, performance analysis and business requirements.
* Monitor the financial impact of unused credits, refunds, cancellations and other recoverable travel value Support strategies to improve Navan adoption and reduce unmanaged/off-platform travel spend

***Stakeholder & Change Management***

* Build strong relationships with Finance, Procurement, Internal Audit, HR, Technology, business leaders and travel stakeholders globally.
* Provide subject-matter expertise and guidance to employees, managers and delegates on T&E processes and policy.
* Support implementation of new T&E technology, policies, controls and operating-model changes.
* Develop communication and training materials and support adoption of new processes.
* Act as a change champion for the ongoing transformation of the T&E programme.

***What Success Looks Like***
***Within the first 12 months, the successful candidate will have:***

* Established a clear T&E governance and compliance framework.
* Created a reliable management dashboard providing visibility of travel spend, compliance, leakage and exceptions.
* Improved control and visibility over travel booked outside approved channels.
* Strengthened pre-trip approval and travel-policy compliance.
* Established a structured process for unused credits, refunds and travel exceptions.
* Identified and implemented high-value automation opportunities that reduce manual controls.
* Established effective governance with TMC and key travel suppliers.
* Built a sustainable T&E operating model with clear ownership, procedures, and reporting.
* Train

title: Contracts Counsel
description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.
  
  
**Job Summary:**
The Contracts Counsel – India will support the Office of General Counsel as the primary point of contact for contract drafting, review, negotiation and contract-related legal support across multiple jurisdictions, including but not limited to US, Canada, El Salvador, India & Chile. The role will provide practical, business-aligned legal advice on a broad range of agreements, including general corporate contracts, employment-related agreements, real estate leases, independent contractor arrangements, extended workforce contracts, vendor agreements, services agreements, NDAs, statements of work, amendments and related documentation.
  
  
This position will partner closely with stakeholders across the General Counsel’s Office, Strategic Sourcing, Talent, Finance, Risk Management, Real Estate/Location Services, IT and business teams to enable timely contracting outcomes, manage legal and commercial risk, improve contract processes and ensure consistency with applicable laws, firm policies, approval requirements and global contracting standards.
  
  
**Essentials**
**Contract Drafting, Review & Negotiation**

* Draft, review, redline and negotiate a broad range of contracts for RSM US LLP and its affiliates across jurisdictions, ensuring clear documentation of rights, obligations, risk allocation and business intent
* Handle general corporate agreements, services agreements, vendor and procurement contracts, NDAs, statements of work, amendments, addenda, order forms and other commercial documentation
* Support employment-related contracts, independent contractor arrangements, extended workforce contracts and staffing/vendor documentation in coordination with Talent, Strategic Sourcing and relevant legal stakeholders
* Review and negotiate real estate leases, leave and license arrangements, facilities-related contracts and location services documentation, coordinating with business and external counsel as needed
* Advise on key contract provisions including indemnities, limitation of liability, confidentiality, data protection, intellectual property, insurance, termination, dispute resolution, governing law, audit rights and compliance obligations
* Negotiate directly with counterparties or their counsel where appropriate and provide practical fallback positions to support efficient deal closure

**Contract Risk Advisory & Legal Support**

* Serve as the sole or primary Office of General Counsel contact for assigned contract matters, ensuring timely triage, review, escalation and resolution
* Provide business-oriented legal advice on contractual risks, deviations from templates, approval requirements and mitigation strategies
* Coordinate with U.S. and international legal stakeholders on matters involving multiple jurisdictions, cross-border contractual obligations or non-standard risk positions
* Identify issues relating to privacy, information security, intellectual property, employment classification, tax, regulatory compliance, procurement, auditor independence and professional standards and route matters to appropriate subject matter experts where needed
* Support contract-related disputes, claims, termination discussions, renewal issues and interpretation questions by reviewing obligations and advising on available contractual remedies
* Ensure contracting positions are consistent with firm policies, delegated authority, risk appetite and applicable legal and regulatory requirements

**Contracting Process, Templates & Knowledge Management**

* Develop, maintain and improve standard contract templates, clause libraries, playbooks, fallback positions and contracting guidance in coordination with the Office of General Counsel and relevant business teams
* Promote consistency in contracting standards, approval processes, records management and use of approved forms across contract types and jurisdictions
* Partner with Strategic Sourcing, Talent, Finance, IT, Real Estate/Location Services, Risk Management and other internal teams to streamline intake, review, negotiation, execution and renewal workflows
* Support adoption and effective use of contract lifecycle management systems, AI contracting tools, tracking tools and reporting mechanisms
* Prepare practical guidance, trainings and communications for stakeholders on contract review requirements, common risk issues and escalation protocols

**Stakeholder Management & Cross-Border Collaboration**

* Build trusted relationships with internal stakeholders and act as a responsive, practical and solutions-oriented legal partner for contracting matters
* Collaborate with attorneys and business teams in the United States, India and other supported jurisdictions to align contracting outcomes with business priorities and legal standards
* Manage competing contract priorities, communicate status clearly and escalate high-risk or time-sensitive issues appropriately
* Support reporting to the Office of General Counsel on contract volumes, risk themes, bottlenecks, improvement opportunities and stakeholder service levels

**Legal Research, Regulatory Awareness & Other Support**

* Monitor legal, regulatory and market developments relevant to contracting, cross-border services, privacy, employment classification, real estate and vendor risk management
* Conduct legal research and prepare concise summaries or recommendations on contract-related legal issues as required
* Support other Office of General Counsel initiatives, special projects and contract-related governance activities as assigned

**EDUCATION/CERTIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor’s degree in Law from a recognized Indian university (required)
* Current Bar Council enrolment or eligibility to practice law in India (required)
* Additional certification or demonstrated training in contract drafting, commercial law, privacy, technology contracting or negotiation (preferred)

**Experience**

* 10 years of post-qualification legal experience, preferably in an in-house legal department, multinational organization, professional services firm or reputed law firm with a strong commercial contracts practice (required)
* Demonstrated experience drafting, reviewing and negotiating commercial agreements, vendor contracts, services agreements, NDAs, statements of work, employment-related agreements and independent contractor arrangements (required)
* Experience advising stakeholders directly on contractual risks, fallback positions, approval requirements and practical negotiation strategy (required)
* Experience supporting cross-border contracting matters or working with international or matrixed legal teams (strongly preferred)
* Experience coordinating with procurement, sourcing, HR/Talent, finance, IT, real estate/location services, risk management and external counsel teams (preferred)
* Exposure to data privacy, information security, auditor independence, professional services, technology, outsourcing or extended workforce contracting issues (preferred

**Leadership Skills**

* Ability to act as a senior individual contributor and trusted legal advisor for contract matters with limited supervision (required)
* Strong stakeholder management skills and ability to build credibility with legal, business and functional leaders across jurisdictions (required)
* Proven ability to prioritize competing requests, manage urgent deadlines and communicate status and risk clearly (required)
* Business-minded, pragmatic and solutions-oriented approach with a strong sense of ownership and accountability (required)
* High degree of integrity, confidentiality, professionalism and sound judgment (required)

**Technical/Soft Skills**

* Strong knowledge of contract law principles and experience with commercial contracting across multiple agreement types and jurisdictions (required)
* Excellent drafting, redlining, negotiation and legal analytical skills, with the ability to identify legal and commercial risks and propose practical solutions (required)
* Working knowledge of key contractual concepts including liability allocation, indemnity, termination, confidentiality, data protection & privacy, intellectual property, service levels, audit rights, insurance, governing law and dispute resolution (required)
* Ability to support contracting matters involving procurement, employment, independent contractors, extended workforce, real estate leases, technology, professional services and general corporate arrangements (most or all areas required)
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain legal concepts and contract risks in concise, business-friendly terms (required)
* High attention to detail, sound judgment, strong ownership and ability to manage multiple matters independently in a deadline-driven environment (required
* Experience effectively leveraging AI tools in connection with contract drafting, redlining, analysis and negotiation (strongly preferred)
* Experience with contract lifecycle management tools, template management, matter tracking and Microsoft Office applications (preferred)
